day_to_day.name: Michi no Eki Asahimachi
day_to_day.description: Asahi is known as the birthplace of bagless-grown Fuji apples. From August to around February the farm-direct corner stocks a changing range of seasonal apples, plus a wide choice of freshly picked vegetables.

day_to_day.name: Wago Midori no Eki
day_to_day.name_ja: 産直「和合みどりの駅」（秋・冬のみ）
day_to_day.description: A seasonal direct-sales stall run by farmer colleagues, open only in autumn and winter. It mainly sells apples, pears and peaches, plus figs, taro and daikon when available.

day_to_day.name: Oishii Dewa Direct Sales Market
day_to_day.name_ja: 産直「おいしい出羽産直市場」
day_to_day.description: A direct-sales market in Asahi selling apples, La France pears, cherries, mountain vegetables, handmade wooden goods, cold-dried rice cakes, pickles and seasonal vegetables.

activities.name: Asahimachi Wine Castle
activities.name_ja: ワイナリー「朝日町ワイン城」
activities.description: Winery based on Yamagata’s climate and long experience, using modern brewing techniques and a one-hectare vineyard of European wine-grape varieties.

activities.name: Ringo Onsen
activities.description: Day-use onsen with strongly alkaline water, uncommon in Tohoku, and a seasonal outdoor bath.

activities.name: Sawaradaira Rice Terraces
activities.description: Terraced paddies on a gentle fan-shaped slope, with reflective water in spring, green fields in summer, golden rice and traditional stake-drying in autumn, and snow in winter. Vehicles cannot pass during snowfall.

activities.name: Imogawa Onsen
activities.description: Day-trip onsen along the clear Asahi River, with free-flowing spring water said to help skin troubles such as heat rash. The owner, who also runs a fishery, serves seafood rice bowls.

activities.name: Mogami River Canoe Land
activities.description: Iogawa Gorge, once a difficult section for boat transport on the Mogami River, is now used for canoeing. From April to around November, canoeists use launch points at Tamanai and Yukitani.

activities.name: Hachimitsu no Mori Candle Workshop
activities.name_ja: 蜜ロウソク工房「ハチ蜜の森キャンドル」
activities.description: Beeswax candle making and beekeeping experiences are offered year-round by reservation, including on weekdays. Off-site classes are also available for children's group events.

activities.name: Asahi Town Tourist Information Center
activities.description: Inside Roadside Station Asahimachi, pamphlets on events and facilities are available and tourism association staff provide guidance. Roadside-station stamp-rally stamps can be collected here.

activities.name: Asahi Shizenkan Ski Area and Cottages
activities.name_en: Asahi Shizenkan Ski Area and Cottages
activities.name_ja: Asahi自然観/スキー場・コテージ
activities.description: Green-season options include barbecues, hiking, trekking, and stream fishing; winter adds skiing and snowboarding at the snow park. The Air Shrine stands in beech forest, and the hotel closed at the end of March 2025.

sights.name: Kuki Shrine (Air Shrine)
sights.description: The only shrine in the world whose object of worship is air itself. It was built in July 1990 to give thanks for the blessings of air and to pass a clean Earth on to future generations; this environmental monument stands in a beech forest.

sights.name: Ostrich Exhibition Field
sights.name_ja: オーストリッチ展示圃
sights.description: Visitors can meet ostriches raised in Asahi, a town known for them.

sights.name: Satake Family Residence
sights.description: A preserved upper-class farmhouse of a village headman who administered an exclave of the Matsuyama Domain Sakai family. It is a National Important Cultural Property, and the Satake family still lives there.

day_to_day.description: Connected to JR Funagata Station, it offers town maps, pamphlets, and tourist information. Soba, udon, soft-serve ice cream, local specialties, and souvenirs are sold, including limited sweets from Wakayu Onsen.

activities.name: Ayu Park Funagata
activities.name_ja: アユパークふながた(河川公園)
activities.description: This riverside park has a large fountain, an imoni plaza, an ayu-shaped channel, rope climbing, and spring play equipment. Shallow areas suit small children, and ayu catching is offered in the channel.

activities.name: Ayukko Village
activities.description: Offers 13 cottages, bungalows, and a ground-tent campsite with space for about eight sites, plus four all-weather tennis courts, two gateball courts, a ground golf course, and a children's play plaza.

activities.name: Funagata Town History and Folklore Museum
activities.name_en: Funagata Town History and Folklore Museum
activities.name_ja: 舟形町歴史民俗資料館
activities.description: Collects, preserves, and displays a replica of the National Treasure clay figurine Jomon no Megami, plus many old documents, folk tools, and folklore materials.

activities.name: Funagata Wakaayu Onsen
activities.description: This onsen emerged in August 1992 and has a large sweetfish sculpture at the entrance. The water contains salt, sodium, and magnesium, and the open-air bath overlooks the town toward Mount Gassan and Hayama.

activities.name: Kenmin Golf Course
activities.description: Eighteen-hole hilly course that uses the land's ups and downs. On clear days, fresh greenery and autumn foliage can be seen.

activities.name: Saruhaneyama Park
activities.description: Seasonal flowers and scenery fill this nature-rich park. Saruhaneyama Jizoson is associated with matchmaking and fertility, and the grounds include a soba restaurant and places to learn history.

activities.name: Kunpukama Pottery Experience
activities.description: Pottery experience using only clay from Funagata, where the national treasure dogu Jomon no Megami was excavated. Hand-building and electric-wheel courses cover cups, plates, nameplates, and dogu replicas.

activities.name: Activity spot in Funagata
activities.description: Said to have been built about 160 years ago as a villa for a sake brewer living in Funagata. The facility can be used for day visits.

activities.name: Tekuramori Wetland
activities.description: Walk 30 minutes on a paved forest road, then about 10 minutes on a side path, to reach a wetland hidden in the forest. Endangered hatcho dragonflies, tokiso, kakiran, and other plants grow there.

sights.name: Sabaneyama Jizoson
sights.description: Counted among Japan's three great Jizo, it has long been worshipped for children, matchmaking and long life; its festival is held on August 24. Next door, Sabaneyama Soba serves hand-made soba milled by the temple's deputy priest, and homemade sesame tofu.

activities.name: Yamagata Airport
activities.description: Yamagata's air gateway, nicknamed Oishii Yamagata Airport. The name reflects the idea that the food, scenery, festivals, and hot springs are all delicious.

activities.name: Long-established fu maker in Higashine
activities.description: Long-established fu maker, one of 400 Yamagata companies operating for over 100 years. Founded in the Bunkyu era, it still makes traditional fu with Rokuda Water in a Japanese-style shop.

activities.name: Donomae Park
activities.description: Urban park east of Higashine Onsen, at the foot of Hebiyama, developed since 1972. About 200 cherry trees and other plants line the path around the pond; an observatory overlooks the Murayama Basin.

activities.name_ja: 黒伏高原スノーパーク ジャングルジャングル
activities.description: 34-hectare ski area facing the cliffs of Mount Kurobushi, with terrain for beginners through advanced. Lessons and rentals are available, snowboarding is allowed on all slopes, and day lift tickets are free through sixth grade.

activities.description: Seasonal fruit picking runs from cherry season and includes cherries, peaches, grapes, and apples. The shop also sells fruit, homemade processed goods, fruit wine, and gift La France pears.

sights.description: A leisure area around a dam built for flood control and irrigation, with seven plazas including a constellation square, a water square, a viewing square, sports grounds, and a stream square with a campground.

sights.description: A low mountain in central Jinmachi has a maintained trail that children can climb. The south-side air-raid shelter is closed but opened once every three years, and the park has fitness equipment.

sights.name: Mount Kurobushi

sights.name: Mountain in Higashine
sights.description: Said to be the prefecture's oldest cliff-carved Buddha, dated to the late Kamakura period. The rock is 5 m high, about 6.5 m wide and 3.5 m thick, with line-carved Buddha images.

sights.name: Funagata Range (Mount Gosho)
sights.description: Centered on Mount Gosho, this range spans Miyagi and Yamagata. Higashine climbs include the Kannonji course, with Yanagisawa Hut mid-slope, a summit shelter, spring alpine plants, and autumn foliage.

sights.name: Iide Michi-no-Eki
sights.description: A products hall on Route 113, midway between the Sea of Japan and the Pacific, selling local souvenirs, folk crafts, sake and fresh vegetables and fruit. The restaurant is popular for its Yonezawa beef bowl and Yonezawa ramen.

sights.name: Shirakawa Dam Kogan Park
sights.description: This is a park around Lake Shirakawa formed by Shirakawa Dam.

sights.name: Donden-daira Snow Park
sights.description: A snow park with snowmobile rides, thrilling banana-boat runs and a giant snow slide, plus snowshoe walks and target-throwing games; guided snowmobile forest rides are available for an extra fee.

sights.name: Shirakawa Lake Submerged Forest
sights.description: For two months in spring, snowmelt fills Shirakawa Lake and willows seem to grow out of the water. From Shirakawa Dam Lakeside Park, early spring looks white and the new-leaf season looks green.

sights.name: Iide Donden-daira Lily Garden
sights.name_ja: いいでどんでん平ゆり園
sights.description: More than 500,000 lilies of many varieties grow here, and a lily festival runs from mid-June to mid-July. The grounds also have seasonal flowers, trees, and a large slide; leashed pets are allowed.

sights.name: Shirakawa Dam
sights.description: A rockfill dam completed in 1981 and standing 66 meters high. Visitors can view the exhibition room, closed in winter, and the crests of the dam and spillway.

sights.name: Hagyu Kannon
sights.name_ja: 大行院 瑞雲寺（真言宗）/ 置賜三十三観音 第11番 萩生観音
sights.description: A Shingon temple and the 11th stop of the Okitama Thirty-three Kannon pilgrimage. It enshrines a wooden seated Eleven-faced Kannon, and a festival is held on July 10.

sights.name: Nagameyama Mizubasho Colony
sights.description: Mizubasho grow wild in a wetland about 500 m long. A walking path follows a small stream, with peak viewing from early April to early May.

day_to_day.description: The roadside station at Kahoku's eastern gateway on Route 287, facing the Mogami River. The ground floor sells souvenirs such as cold meat soba and the town's slippers, local sake and light meals, and has tourist information.

day_to_day.name_ja: アグリランド ひな産直センター
day_to_day.description: A direct-sales shop opposite Hinano-yu in Kahoku, selling seasonal local vegetables and fruit, including Kahoku Italian vegetables and town-made slippers. A gelato corner and a Sunday market are on site.

activities.name: Kahoku Town Children's Zoo
activities.description: More than 30 kinds of animals are kept, including a toco toucan, hedgehogs, deer, ponies, monkeys, goats, sheep, rabbits, and owls. Open year-round, 24 hours, with free admission.

activities.name: Kahoku Central Park (Imoko Train)
activities.name_ja: 河北中央公園（いもこ列車）
activities.description: Set near the center of Kahoku on about 5 hectares, with water and land field athletics, wooden play equipment, and tennis courts.

activities.name: Benibana Onsen Hinano-yu
activities.description: Opened in June 1999, with a sauna and access for people with disabilities. Restaurant Yuratei offers meals and takeout, and neighboring Hinano-yado has overnight stays with two meals.

activities.name: Benibana Museum / Former Horigome Residence
activities.description: The former Horigome Residence of a wealthy safflower merchant was restored and opened as a museum in May 1984. Edo-period Mogami safflower petals were made into flower cakes and sent to Kyoto.

activities.name: Kahoku Roadside Station Buratto Pia
activities.name_ja: 道の駅 河北 ～ ぶらっとぴあ ～
activities.description: On National Route 287 at Kahoku's eastern entrance, facing the Mogami River. The first floor offers tourist information and sells cold meat soba, slippers, local sake, and light meals.

activities.name: Kahoku Town General Exchange Center Sahato Benibana
activities.name_en: Kahoku Town General Exchange Center Sahato Benibana
activities.name_ja: 河北町総合交流センター サハトべに花
activities.description: Named Sahato, Arabic for plaza, because safflower is said to originate in Egypt. The town is known as the home of hina dolls and safflower.

activities.name: Mogami River Green Park
activities.name_ja: 最上川グリーンパーク
activities.description: Near Yachi Bridge on the Mogami River, with a golf course and several plazas. Wanpaku Plaza sits just below Roadside Station Buratto Pia, along with Fureai Plaza, Yasuragi Plaza, and a multipurpose sports plaza.

activities.name: Ebitsuru Onsen
activities.description: Hot spring linked to a Kahoku legend, just below the embankment after Kahoku Bridge across the Mogami River. The site once farmed edible tilapia, an introduced fish, and photos are displayed inside.

activities.name: Sun Sport Land Kahoku

activities.description: Baseball field called Rakuten Eagles Benibana Stadium Kahoku, four tennis courts, and Fureai Plaza on a 45,910-square-meter site. Spectator capacity is 5,000, and the facilities are used from April to November.

activities.name: Kahoku Municipal Pool
activities.description: Indoor pool for aqua walking that uses water resistance, with jets for the back, waist, and shoulders expected to promote circulation. A training room has treadmills and fitness bikes adjusted to each person's fitness.

sights.description: The restored residence of the Horigome family, wealthy safflower merchants, opened as a safflower museum in 1984. In the Edo period the local Mogami safflower was made into dried petal cakes and shipped all the way to Kyoto.

activities.name: Zao Raiza World
activities.description: A family ski area near a rime-ice forest, with a wide 570 m course plus beginner, intermediate, and advanced runs. Weekend sledding beside the restaurant is planned when snow allows.

activities.name: Kimura Tourist Orchard
activities.description: Visitors can pick cherries, grapes, and apples in season. The orchard also grows and sells those fruits, along with La France pears.

activities.name: Woody Farm & Winery
activities.name_ja: ウッディファーム＆ワイナリー
activities.description: A domaine winery on the Zao foothills grows nine grape varieties and handles winemaking and bottling. Wine tastings need no reservation, while winery tours with tastings are offered by reservation.

activities.name: DROP
activities.description: A winery opened in town in 2023 by a grower who began cultivating wine grapes in 2019. An attached wine stand lets visitors taste natural wines expressing the vineyard's four seasons.

activities.name: Saito Tourist Fruit Orchard
activities.description: Cherries and apples can be picked on a spacious flat orchard accessible to older visitors and people with limited mobility. Cherries, apples, and European pears are also sold, and groups are welcome.

activities.name: ZAO Tairagura
activities.description: A comprehensive exchange facility at Zao Bodaira with a training room used for camps in many sports. It also has a farm-produce direct-sales shop, an experience room, and a cooking practice room.

activities.name: Himawari Farm
activities.description: Cherries can be picked, and La France pears are also grown. Cherries, apples, and European pears are sold, with a shop for purchases after picking.

activities.name: Zao Sarukura Ski Area

sights.name: Kaminoyama Castle Local Museum
sights.description: Kaminoyama Castle, also called Tsukioka Castle, is said to have been built in 1535. It was the southernmost stronghold of the Mogami clan and saw fighting with the Date and Uesugi of Yonezawa; today it houses the local history museum.

sights.name: Takahashi Fruits Land HATAKE STYLE
sights.description: An orchard growing seasonal fruit 100% organically, with greenhouse cherries for early cherry picking. The adjoining HATAKE STYLE café serves parfaits, sundaes and soft-serve.

sights.name: Narage-juku (Ushu Kaido Post Town)
sights.description: A post town on the Ushu Kaido that once bustled with daimyo processions, with a main inn, sub-inn and lodging houses. Old houses and stone bridges line the river, and some of the old houses are open to visitors.

sights.name: Kaminoyama Domain Samurai Residences
sights.description: Four thatched samurai houses of the Kaminoyama domain, about 200 years old, stand in a row. The Miwa interior is open to visitors; Morimoto, Yamada, and the former Sogabe show exteriors and gardens.

sights.name: Zao Katta Lift
sights.description: A lift to Okama, a crater lake among Mount Katta, Mount Kumano, and Mount Goshiki. Its emerald water changes color with the light; at 10 meters the water is about 2°C and warms with depth.

sights.name: Shimo-Oyu Communal Bath
sights.description: A communal bath in Kaminoyama Onsen, opened in 1624 by domain lord Matsudaira and said to have been used by Zen master Takuan. Hot and lukewarm tubs remain, and 2024 marked 400 years since opening.

sights.name: Hanasakiyama Observatory
sights.name_ja: 花咲山展望台（恋人の聖地）
sights.description: A viewpoint on the Hayama course near Hayama Onsen, with views of the town and the Zao range through the seasons. Hydrangeas bloom in summer, and the walk from the trailhead takes about 30 minutes.

sights.name: Harusame Hermitage
sights.description: Priest Takuan, known for takuan pickles, spent three years here after exile to Kaminoyama in 1629. The restored building is a prefectural Important Cultural Property, with the Harusame well and Choutei tea room.

sights.name: Tsukioka Park
sights.description: A cherry-blossom park in Kaminoyama centered on Kaminoyama Castle, with about 80 trees including old Somei-yoshino, weeping cherries, and a few Keio-zakura. A nearby foot bath looks toward the Zao range.

sights.name: Former Ogata Family Residence
sights.description: Built around the mid-17th century for the Ogata family, hereditary village headmen, this farmhouse uses nail-free construction and is a National Important Cultural Property. It is temporarily closed.

sights.name: Local sight in Kaminoyama
sights.name_ja: ヴェンテンガルテン 菜の花畑
sights.description: A citizen farm near JR Mokichi Memorial Hall Station has a heart-shaped rapeseed field, heart-shaped photo frames, and views of the Zao range. Flowers usually bloom from late April to early May.

sights.name: Zao Senninzawa Ice Garden Icefall
sights.name_ja: 蔵王 仙人沢アイスガーデンの氷瀑
sights.description: Ice formations appear only in midwinter at Senninzawa on Bodaira Plateau in Kaminoyama. The main icefall is about 30 meters high and tens of meters wide, seen from January to mid-March.

sights.name: Kurikawa Inari Shrine
sights.description: It enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto, guardian deity of the Fujii Matsudaira family and long worshipped by successive castle lords. Donated torii form a tunnel-like approach; the annual festival is held on April 23.

sights.name: Kurort Hayama Course
sights.name_ja: クアオルト 葉山コース
sights.description: Locals have planted cherries, autumn leaves, and hydrangeas along this walking course near the onsen district since 2007. Hanasakiyama Observatory, designated a Lover's Sanctuary, overlooks the town and the Zao range.

sights.name: Tsukioka Shrine
sights.description: It enshrines members of the Matsudaira domain family. The annual festival is on April 25, a special festival is held with Hachiman Shrine in mid-September, and shrine seals are available.

sights.name: Kaminoyama Castle Foot Bath
sights.description: A foot bath beside Kaminoyama Castle overlooks the city and the Zao mountain range. In spring it can be used while viewing cherry blossoms.

sights.name: Maekawa Foot Bath
sights.description: A foot bath at the base of Mayukawa Bridge and the closest to JR Kaminoyama-Onsen Station. It is a place to rest while waiting for a train or shinkansen.

sights.name: Shinyu Foot Bath
sights.description: A foot bath in the Shinyu Onsen town, opened in 1953 and used by tourists and local residents. A foot-bath stamp is available.

sights.name: Yumachi Foot Bath (Crane's Resting Stone)
sights.description: A foot bath at the birthplace of Kaminoyama Onsen, in the quiet Yumachi hot-spring district. The Crane's Resting Stone stands on the grounds, and a hand bath is also available.

sights.name: Saito Mokichi Poem Monument at Zao Kumanodake Summit
sights.name_en: Saito Mokichi Poem Monument at Zao Kumanodake Summit
sights.name_ja: 斎藤茂吉歌碑/蔵王熊野岳山頂
sights.description: A poem stone erected in August 1934 atop Zao Kumanodake, the only monument Mokichi approved in his lifetime. It faces his birthplace in Kanakame, Kaminoyama; he first saw it on 8 July 1939.

sights.name: Kurort Nishiyama Course
sights.name_ja: クアオルト 西山コース
sights.description: A satoyama course about 15 minutes' walk from the station, passing mountains around 300 meters with views of the Zao range and town, poet monuments, and traces of old terraced fields.

sights.name: DEEP ZAO: Juhyo Field of Zao Bodaira Plateau
sights.name_en: DEEP ZAO: Juhyo Field of Zao Bodaira Plateau
sights.name_ja: DEEP ZAO 蔵王坊平高原の樹氷原
sights.description: On Kaminoyama's Bodaira Plateau in the Zao range, summer brings alpine plants at Otanokami Marsh, and winter winds from the Iide and Asahi ranges form juhyo, with beech forest beyond.

sights.name: Hosenji Temple
sights.description: The family temple of the poet Saito Mokichi, in Kanakame, Kaminoyama, his hometown.

sights.name: Born here in Kaminoyama
sights.description: Born here on 14 May in Meiji 15 (1882) as the third son of Moriya Den'emon. The house is private, and only the exterior may be viewed.

sights.name: Hayama Foot Bath (Yuami Jizo)
sights.description: A foot bath on a hill in the Hayama Onsen district, which opened in 1936. It overlooks the town and the Zao range, and a foot-bath stamp is available.

sights.name: Saito Mokichi Poem Monuments / Tsukioka Park
sights.name_en: Saito Mokichi Poem Monuments / Tsukioka Park
sights.name_ja: 斎藤茂吉歌碑/月岡公園
sights.description: Poem stones by Saito Mokichi stand in Tsukioka Park, raised in 1961 for the city's seventh anniversary and in 1972 by Kaminoyama Rotary Club. One recalls his mother; one followed a climb of Mt. Kokuzo.

sights.name: Takamatsu Kannon
sights.name_ja: 高松山 光明院（真言宗）/ 最上三十三観音 第11番 高松観音
sights.description: A Shingon temple and the 11th stop of the Mogami Thirty-three Kannon pilgrimage. It enshrines a tiny seated Sho-Kannon attributed to Gyoki, and naked rice-cake pounding is offered each December.

sights.name: Kannon Falls
sights.description: An 80-meter straight waterfall in Senninzawa Gorge on the Zao Bodaira plateau. Entry is currently prohibited because part of the trail and cliff has collapsed; the stated season is mid-May to early November.

sights.name: Kurort Oshimizu-Juhyogen Course
sights.name_ja: クアオルト お清水・樹氷原コース
sights.description: Once a departure point for Zao mountain worship, the course passes stone Buddhas, Zao Gongen, and a poem monument. In winter, Aomori firs become rime-ice trees, and clear days open views toward Mount Chokai.

sights.name: Saiko-ji Temple
sights.description: A temple with a vermilion gate that cherry blossoms cover at full bloom. The tree, one of the largest crowns in the city, is a municipal preserved tree.

activities.description: Log house for considering what a rich life in a mountain village means. Traditional indigo dyeing, maple-sap collection, forest play, and forest making convey forest living, and wild itaya maple sap is boiled down.

activities.description: The grounds cover about 25,000 tsubo, with a horse ranch, fishing, lawn activities, family visits, and forest-road walks. Former Kamuro training-farm buildings include circular wooden architecture.

activities.name: Yugaku Forest
activities.description: Yamagata Prefecture's fourth prefectural forest, it draws on the Mogami region's nature and local culture. The guiding idea is a model area where forests and people coexist, with nature-learning facilities planned.

activities.name: Yawata Park
activities.description: Redeveloped in 1995 beside Yawata Shrine, it replaced a little-used children's park with a design that uses water. Gently rolling lawns lie inland, reached by a pond-side path from the road.

sights.description: Irrigation canal around central Kaneyama, built over seven years from 1977 to 1983. Rough-cut stone forms the bed and sides, and perforated blocks let water seep underground.

sights.name: Daimiwa Giant Cedar
sights.description: Said to have been planted since the domain era. Nearly 300 years old, the giant cedar at Daimiwa in Ariya stands in 0.87 hectares of Kaneyama cedar with 115 trees.

sights.name: Kaneyama Three Peaks
sights.name_ja: 金山三峰（薬師山・中の森・熊鷹森）
sights.description: Three pyramid-shaped peaks seen from Kamiage Pass on National Route 13, listed from the west: Yakushi-yama (436.7 m), Naka-no-Mori (415 m), and Kumataka-mori (390 m).

sights.name: Townscape of Gabled Roofs and White Walls
sights.name_en: Townscape of Gabled Roofs and White Walls
sights.name_ja: 切妻屋根と白壁の町並み
sights.description: Local Kaneyama cedar is used in Kaneyama houses, forming streets of white walls and gabled roofs. Materials suited to the climate age beautifully and give a nostalgic, refined look.

sights.name: Megane Weir
sights.description: Water from the Kamuro mountains flows through this weir. Residents work on shaping the surrounding landscape.

sights.name: Taniguchi Silver Mine Site
sights.description: The mine peaked in the early Shinjo domain years, about 1624-1651, with 66 tunnels. Records say seven cattle carried 120 kg of silver daily for seven months to refining, until flooding in 1662.

sights.name: Ogiri Falls
sights.description: Waterfall beside the Taniguchi Silver Mine ruins that slides down among trees. The drop is about 20 meters. The beginner route takes five minutes from the parking area and includes a steep slope.

sights.name: Suwa Shrine

sights.name: Tenjinmori Kofun

sights.description: Views of Mt. Chokai and the Dewa Hills, unusual rocks, and alpine plants. The trail to the col between Otoko and Onna Kamuyama has a narrow steep section called Tainai-kuguri, then a difficult summit route.

sights.name: Sangai Falls
sights.description: Tiered waterfall about 5 meters high, with a broad, cool, pool-like basin. Beginner difficulty; about one minute from beside a forest road, viewed from below the falls.

day_to_day.name_en: Semi Onsen Communal Bath Semi no Yu
day_to_day.name_ja: 瀬見温泉共同浴場 せみの湯
day_to_day.description: Indoor, steam-heated, and outdoor baths can be used together. The indoor pools are hot and moderate with little added water, and a covered foot bath and hot-spring egg space are available.

day_to_day.description: Opened on 26 November 2023, it shares tourism, event, and road information for Mogami Town and nearby municipalities. Attse is Mogami dialect meaning that something is available, used when offering tea, food, or rest.

activities.name: Semi Onsen
activities.description: A quiet hot-spring town on the Oguni River, long known as Shinjo's retreat. Legend says it was discovered by Minamoto no Yoshitsune's party as they fled toward Hiraizumi.

sights.name: Sakaida Watershed
sights.description: In the plaza before JR Rikuu East Line Sakaida Station, water from the north splits east to the Pacific and west to the Sea of Japan. This flatland divide is closed November to March.

sights.name: Akakura Onsen
sights.description: A hot-spring area in Mogami with free-flowing source water, traditionally opened in 863 by the priest Jikaku Daishi. The water is a sodium-calcium-sulfate spring, and each inn uses its own source.

sights.name: Natagiri Pass
sights.description: Matsuo Basho and Kawai Sora crossed this pass in 1689 toward Obanazawa on the Oku no Hosomichi route. Views include the Kamuro range and Mount Gassan, and a winding beech-forest path follows Basho's route.

sights.name: Former Ariji Family Residence (Hojin no Ie)
sights.name_en: Former Ariji Family Residence (Hojin no Ie)
sights.name_ja: 旧有路家住宅（封人の家）
sights.description: This thatched hipped-roof hall-type farmhouse was designated a National Important Cultural Property in 1969 and restored for public viewing. It is regarded as the border official’s house in Sakaida where Matsuo Basho stayed.

sights.name: Maemori Plateau
sights.description: A 200-hectare plateau with cottages, horseback-riding facilities, and a place serving handmade soba, set in open grassland.

sights.name: Semi Gorge
sights.description: Runs about 4 km up and down National Route 47 along the Mogami Oguni River, centered on Semi Onsen. Spring greenery, autumn leaves, and year-round fishing, especially Matsubara ayu, are noted.

sights.name: Mogami Shirakawa Stream and Shirakawa Dam Park
sights.name_en: Mogami Shirakawa Stream and Shirakawa Dam Park
sights.name_ja: 最上白川渓流・白川ダム公園
sights.description: Shirakawa Dam is 273 meters long and 12 meters high on the upper Shirakawa, at the foot of the Kamuro range. Nearby are autumn foliage, streamside forest walks, and a downstream park used for camping.

sights.name: Atagoyama Park
sights.description: 200 Somei-Yoshino and mountain cherry trees bloom here and are illuminated during the cherry festival. Azaleas, bush clover, and hydrangeas flower at different times through the year.

sights.name: Oku no Hosomichi Akakura Yukemuri-kan Day Onsen
sights.name_en: Oku no Hosomichi Akakura Yukemuri-kan Day Onsen
sights.name_ja: 日帰り温泉「おくのほそ道」赤倉ゆけむり館
sights.description: A day-trip hot spring with an open-air bath in a Japanese garden, family baths, and a produce and community space. The garden changes with the seasons of the Mogami area.

day_to_day.name: Michi-no-Eki Murayama
day_to_day.description: A roadside station in Murayama, at the centre of Yamagata Prefecture, with parking on both sides of the road linked by a footbridge. It stocks Yamagata sake, sweets and specialities, and a farm stand sells seasonal produce.

activities.name: Activity spot in Murayama
activities.description: Lake, river, gorge or waterfall in Murayama, Yamagata.

activities.name: Higashisawa Rose Park
activities.description: Colorful roses bloom across the grounds beyond the entrance. About 20,000 rose bushes fill the park, and the Rose Exchange Hall sells soft-serve ice cream made with roses.

activities.name: Kurhaus Goten
activities.description: Ten baths can be chosen by their effects, and a Western-style outdoor spa pool is available. The restaurant serves country soba made with Murayama-grown Dewakaori buckwheat flour.

activities.name: Yubunezawa Onsen
activities.description: Surrounded by greenery, this single mountain inn has warming water called beauty water. Meals use natural ingredients year-round, fireflies appear in early summer, and a thatched-roof building dates from 1875.

activities.name: Soba-Making Experience / Rural Tradition House
activities.name_ja: そば打ち体験/農村伝承の家
activities.description: At the Rural Culture Preservation Hall, visitors make soba with a soba master's guidance and can eat what they prepare. Folk tools and crafts from the countryside are displayed.

activities.name: Natural Junsai Picking Experience
activities.name_ja: 天然ジュンサイの摘みとり体験
activities.description: Natural junsai is picked at Oyachi Marsh, commonly called Junsai Marsh. Plants here are thick, rich in jelly-like nuru, and very soft, and picking is limited to early summer.

activities.name: Horse Garden Murayama
activities.name_ja: ホースガーデンむらやま
activities.description: Set in quiet countryside north of Murayama, horseback riding is available among green fields. Professional instructors are present, so beginners can ride.

activities.name: Mogami River Art Museum
activities.description: Paintings by Keiji Mashimo, who loved and continued to paint the Mogami River, can be viewed with the river. The permanent exhibition room uses natural light and wire-free displays.

activities.name: Cloisonne Experience
activities.description: Glass glaze is applied to metal such as copper plate and fired at about 800 degrees. Wired cloisonne brought from Tang China in the Nara period was treasured as a secret heirloom.

activities.name: Higashizawa Boat House
activities.description: A boat house in Higashizawa Park offers rental boats and light meals. Seasonal scenery can be viewed along the lakeshore.

activities.name: Toshu Kiln Goten-yaki
activities.description: A pottery kiln a two-minute walk from Goten, one of three difficult points on the Mogami River. Visitors from beginners to experienced makers can create their own pieces, including bluish Ai and iron-glaze Ginsuna ware.

sights.name: Higashizawa Rose Park
sights.description: Beyond the entrance, beds of colourful roses bloom across the park: about 20,000 rose bushes. The Rose Exchange Hall sells a popular rose soft-serve ice cream.

sights.name: Hayashizaki Iai Shrine
sights.description: The only shrine in Japan dedicated to iai, enshrining Hayashizaki Jinsuke Shigenobu, founder of iaido. Each September practitioners of many schools give demonstrations, and visitors can join an iaido experience programme.

sights.name: Shorenzan Seijoin (Komatsuzawa Kannon)
sights.name_ja: 青蓮山 清浄院（真言宗）/ 最上三十三観音 第20番 小松沢観音
sights.description: A Shingon temple, the 20th of the Mogami 33 Kannon pilgrimage. The approach climbs about 1.5 km and 164 stone steps; giant straw sandals hang at the gate, and mukasari wedding plaques fill the hall.

sights.name: Yuki no Kannon / Fubo Hoonji Temple
sights.name_en: Yuki no Kannon / Fubo Hoonji Temple
sights.description: A temple hall built by Diet member Matsuoka Shunzo and named for prayers connected to his snow-damage relief campaign. An account says prayer to the Kannon he carried made a blizzard near Aomori subside.

sights.name: Fubo Hoonji Temple
sights.description: A Jodo sect temple built to guard Suwayama Cemetery and named to honor deceased parents. Its copper seated Amida, made in 1715, is a Murayama City cultural property.

stays.description: Hotel in Murayama, Yamagata.

stays.name_ja: クアハウス碁点
stays.description: Kuahausu in Goten, Murayama, with a pool, large public bath, sauna, and open-air bath overlooking the Mogami River.

day_to_day.name: Michi no Eki Kawano Minato Nagai
day_to_day.description: Nagai's gateway roadside station, with tourist information and local specialities. A food corner serves dishes and sweets made from local produce, and a market stall sells fresh vegetables.

activities.name: Mibuchi Gorge Through-Passage Worship
activities.name_ja: 絶景・三淵渓谷通り抜け参拝
activities.description: Mibuchi Gorge on Nagai Hyakushuko can be seen only by boat, on a passage of about one hour. It also draws visitors as a power spot.

activities.name: Nagai Dam / Nagai Hyakushuko
activities.name_ja: 長井ダム／ながい百秋湖
activities.description: Completed in 2011 a short climb west of central Nagai, the dam created Nagai Hyakushuko. The lake scenery is especially beautiful in the fresh-green and autumn-foliage seasons.

activities.name: Nagai Hyakushuko Matsuri
activities.description: Observation point in Nagai, Yamagata.

activities.name: Nogawa Manabi-kan
activities.description: Lake, river, gorge or waterfall in Nagai, Yamagata.

activities.name: Kodai no Oka
activities.description: At the foot of the Asahi mountains in Kusaoka, sites span the Paleolithic to the Sengoku period. Dogu Plaza has enlarged, restored clay figurines, plus Choja Yashiki materials and city excavation finds.

activities.name: Nagai Ayame Festival
activities.description: More than several hundred flower varieties bloom in the 3.3-hectare park, including Nagai koshu irises seen only there. The season runs from mid-June to early July.

activities.name: Nagai Ayame Onsen New Sakurayu
activities.name_ja: 長井あやめ温泉「ニュー桜湯」
activities.description: About 5 km west of Route 287 (Nagai Ohashi) at 265 m, it overlooks Nagai and the Okitama Basin from the Asahi mountains. The free-flowing, iron-rich water is faintly brown and leaves the body warm.

activities.name: Nagai Ayame Park
activities.description: More than several hundred iris varieties bloom in a park open for over 110 years; ayame is a symbol of Nagai. Flowers are in season from mid-June to early July.

activities.name: Unohana Onsen Haginoyu
activities.name_ja: 卯の花温泉 はぎ乃湯
activities.description: Spring water from the source supplies the large bath and an unusual outdoor bath. A bedrock bath, shop, lounge, rest room, dining area, and massage corners are also on site.

activities.name: Doshojidaira Ski Area
activities.description: A ski area in Hirayama, Nagai. The 2025-26 season is scheduled from December 25 to March 1, and dates may change with snowfall.

activities.name: Nagai Hyakushuko Sightseeing Boat
activities.name_ja: 【2026年中止】ながい百秋湖 遊覧船
activities.description: Boat cruises for autumn foliage on Nagai Hyakushuko at Nagai Dam are not operating in 2026. An amphibious bus runs from September to early November instead.

activities.name: Ishibuchi Buggy Challenge
activities.name_ja: いしぶちバギーチャレンジ
activities.description: An off-road buggy activity based at Nogawa Manabikan. Drivers must be of junior high school age or older, younger children need a parent, and the route pairs a short safety course with a longer course.

activities.name: Yamagata Morimori Forest
activities.name_ja: やまがたもりもりの森
activities.description: A satoyama forest base centered on a colorful treehouse, offering forest play, countryside experiences, and day camping. Seasonal activities include meeting chickens and gathering wild plants, mushrooms, and maple sap.

activities.name: Kendama Plaza SPIKe
activities.description: In Nagai, which produces about 70 percent of Japan's competition kendama, visitors can try them, watch technique videos, and receive grade or rank certificates. Kendama, holders, and a painting experience are also available.

sights.name_en: Former Nagai Elementary School First Building
sights.name_ja: 旧長井小学校第一校舎
sights.description: Built in 1933 beside Nagai City Hall, this two-story wooden schoolhouse was registered as a national tangible cultural property in 2009. It has a reddish exterior, large central staircase, and long boat-bottom-ceiling corridor.

sights.name: Sangai Falls (Fudo Falls)
sights.description: A three-tier waterfall in Kuwazawa, Teraiizumi, Nagai, on a former pilgrimage shortcut toward Mount Iwaigame. The surroundings have fresh greenery and autumn foliage, and the narrow access road closes in winter.

sights.name: Local sight in Nagai
sights.name_ja: 最上川ビューポイント（最上川発祥の地）
sights.description: The Matsukawa and Oitama Shirakawa meet here, and the river takes the name Mogami. It is the first prefecture-selected Mogami River Viewpoint, with a footpath, cherry trees and a trolley path.

sights.name: Kotai Shrine
sights.description: A shrine beside White Azalea Park enshrining Amaterasu, with a hall from Ise Grand Shrine, as Okitama's tutelary shrine. Founding records burned in 1864. The Koide lion dance here is a city intangible cultural property.

sights.name: Saito Family Residence
sights.description: A late-Edo thatched two-story wooden townhouse with a Meiji-period storehouse, preserved along the old street. It is a nationally registered tangible cultural property and is not open to the public.

sights.name: Kodai no Oka Museum
sights.description: Displays finds from the mid-Jomon Chojayashiki site and other city ruins. Nearby are a Jomon soba hall, a dogu plaza, and a sun plaza, with a Jomon festival each October.

sights.name: Hayama Forest Park
sights.description: A forest campsite among cedar woods, with a stream for water play and shared bungalows. Views open toward Asahi, Iide, Zao, and Azuma, and autumn brings colored foliage.

sights.name: Mogami River Footpath
sights.description: A path for strolling along the Mogami River and town waterside lanes, completed in June 2005. Wooden bridges, stepping stones, and signs were added on the left bank between the Shirakawa and Nogawa confluences.

sights.name: Hagi Park
sights.description: White and red bush clover flower from early August to mid-September. Irises, azaleas, maples, roses, bamboo, cedar, and Japanese cypress also grow here, next to Unohana Onsen Haginoyu.

sights.name: Former Marudai Ogiya (Bunkyo-no-Mori)
sights.description: A merchant house that prospered on Mogami River boat transport from the Edo through Showa periods, spanning about 330 years. Seven buildings remain and it was designated a Yamagata Prefecture tangible cultural property in 2003.

sights.name: Kuwajima Memorial Hall (Former Kuwajima Eye Clinic)
sights.name_en: Kuwajima Memorial Hall (Former Kuwajima Eye Clinic)
sights.name_ja: 桑島記念館（旧桑島眼科医院）
sights.description: A wooden two-story Western-style building constructed in 1927 as an eye clinic and designated a city tangible cultural property. After a citizen campaign, it was moved to a corner of Honmachi parking lot and preserved.

sights.name: Unnan Shrine
sights.description: A shrine honoring Fujiwara Unnan, who settled the Gangyo Rebellion of 878 without forcing military service. Two cedars estimated at about 600 years old, designated a natural monument in 1978, stand along the approach.

sights.name: Mount Iwaigame
sights.description: A steep mountain of 1,417 m, counted among Japan's 300 famous mountains and called Tohoku's Matterhorn. Its northern ridge is in Bandai-Asahi National Park, and citizen climbs are held in the fresh-green and autumn-foliage seasons.

sights.name: Kusaoka no Daimyojin Zakura
sights.description: Nationally designated natural monument cherry about 1,200 years old, 14 m tall with a 27 m branch spread, growing at a private home. Locally called the sowing cherry because it blooms near spring planting time.

activities.name: Activity spot in Nakayama
activities.name_ja: 芋煮会発祥の地 中山町
activities.description: The Mogami River flows north through Yamagata to the Sea of Japan. Edo-period boats carried rice, safflower, and ramie via Sakata toward Kyoto and Osaka, returning with sugar, dried fish, clothing, and hina dolls.

activities.name: Himawari Onsen Yurara
activities.name_ja: ひまわり温泉 ゆ・ら・ら
activities.description: Public lodging opened in December 1993. The JR Aterazawa Line Mogami River Bridge to the north, once one bridge with the Flower Nagai Line Arato Bridge, is Japan's oldest railway bridge still in use.

activities.name: Nakayama Park
activities.description: Sports park centered on Yamaryo Stadium Yamagata, the prefectural baseball field, plus a second baseball field and multipurpose plaza. Farmland surrounds it, and the stadium is visible from National Route 112.

activities.name: Himawari Ground Golf Course
activities.name_ja: ひまわりグラウンド・ゴルフ場
activities.description: Dedicated ground-golf course in Mogami River Nakayama Green Space, with six courses and 48 holes, certified by the Japan Ground Golf Association. Mount Gassan and Mount Zao can be seen, and national tournaments are held.

activities.name: Former Nagasaki School Entrance
activities.description: Early Meiji entrance, relocated to the town history and folklore museum. Saigo Tsugumichi, then navy vice admiral and Minister of Agriculture and Commerce, addressed the Nagasaki Elementary opening from this white balcony.

activities.name: Mogami River Nakayama Green Space
activities.name_ja: 最上川中山緑地(運動広場など）
activities.description: West of Nagasaki Bridge are a sports ground for softball, soccer and baseball, tennis courts and a children's plaza. A cycling path, open plaza, flower beds and picnic areas are also here.

sights.name_ja: 金剛山 正法寺（真言宗）/ 最上三十三観音 第14番岡村観音
sights.description: Fourteenth of the Mogami 33 Kannon, this Shingon temple's origin story tells that priest Gyoki carved a sandalwood Kannon in the Nara period and prayed for rain during a drought.

sights.name: Nakayama Town History and Folklore Museum
sights.name_en: Nakayama Town History and Folklore Museum
sights.name_ja: 中山町立歴史民俗資料館
sights.description: About 3,000 items cover inland farming, Mogami River shipping, daily life, and Important Cultural Property materials on Iwaya Juhachiya Kannon folk belief. Nagasaki Elementary School's early Meiji entrance, a town cultural property, was moved here.

sights.name: Darumadera Temple
sights.description: Soto Zen temple founded in 1616. The gate, received from Tendo Atago Jizo Gongen under the Shinto-Buddhist separation edict, shows late Edo features. Inside are an Iki Daruma scroll and a Tsunbuku Daruma figure.

sights.name: Tate Inari Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 1472 from a divided spirit of Kyoto's Fushimi Inari, said to be a prayer for residents' prosperity. The festival is on September 9.

sights.name: Former Kashiwagura Soemon Family Residence
sights.name_ja: 旧柏倉惣右衛門家住宅
sights.description: The main house, built from 1920 to 1922 on about 1,600 tsubo, belongs to a 1724 branch of the Kashiwagura Kyuzaemon family that served as village head. Nakayama Town designates it a tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Koshuin Temple (Seated Dainichi Nyorai)
sights.description: Founded in 1560 by shugen ascetic Samon, this Tendai Jimon temple is a town tangible cultural property. Its bronze seated Dainichi Nyorai, cast in 1768, stands 2.8 meters high.

sights.name: Koshoji Temple
sights.description: Established in 1667, this Jodo Shinshu Honganji sect temple enshrines a wooden Amida Nyorai carved by Koun as its principal image.

sights.name: Important Cultural Property Former Kashiwagura Family Residence (Kyuzaemon)
sights.name_en: Important Cultural Property Former Kashiwagura Family Residence (Kyuzaemon)
sights.name_ja: 重要文化財 旧柏倉家住宅（九左衛門）
sights.description: This large residence inherits the form of an early-modern upper-class farmhouse. The present main house comes from a predecessor built in 1783, after a major renovation in 1898, with precious-wood rooms, lacquer, and gold leaf.

sights.description: Shinto shrine in Nakayama, Yamagata.

sights.name: Nabekake Pine
sights.description: This fifth-generation pine marks where boatmen and merchants began imoni gatherings, cooking salted cod and taro in pots hung from branches while waiting to transfer cargo at the former Mogami River terminus.

day_to_day.name: Sakai Winery
day_to_day.description: Founded in 1892, the oldest winery in Tohoku, still making wine the traditional way: unfiltered, unfined and unpasteurised. Since 2004 the family has farmed its own steep, gravelly vineyard at Torigozaka.

day_to_day.description: A public bath that opened in June 2022, with barrier-free bathing rooms. Soap and shampoo are not set out in the baths but are included with admission.

activities.name_en: Balloon Flight Experience at Jubuichiyama Famous for Sea of Clouds
activities.name_ja: 雲海で有名な十分一山での気球フライト体験
activities.description: A rope-tethered balloon rises about 15-20 meters at Jubuichiyama in Nanyo, overlooking the Okitama Basin, nearby 2,000-meter peaks, and sometimes a sea of clouds. Boarding-only and full-participation options are available.

activities.name: Suto Wine Factory
activities.description: A family winery handles cultivation, harvest, brewing, and bottling itself. Its Shikin-en vineyard offers grape picking from early August to mid-October, and a harvest-to-wine experience from mid-August to early October.

activities.name: Oura Wine
activities.description: Wine production began here in 1939 in Nanyo, called the birthplace of Yamagata grapes. Wines range from sweet, fruity types to richer aged ones, with attention to each grape variety's character.

activities.name: Matsuda Tourist Fruit Orchard
activities.name_ja: （ヤマ松） 松田観光果樹園
activities.description: A tourist fruit orchard in Nanyo. The city grows cherries such as Sato Nishiki and Benishuho, and its tourist orchards and farm shops are busy from June to early July.

activities.name: Daimaru Farm
activities.description: In Nanyo, one of Yamagata’s main cherry-producing areas, varieties such as Sato Nishiki and Benishuho are grown. Tourist cherry orchards and direct-sales shops are busy from June to early July.

activities.name: Maruen Endo Farm

sights.description: Set on a hill overlooking the Yonezawa Basin and known as the 'rose garden of fragrance', with 6,000 roses of 340 varieties, including many rare old roses. Kumano Taisha shrine is nearby.

sights.name: Kuguri Fall
sights.description: A 14 m waterfall in Nanyo's Kotaki district that pours through a hole in the rock 5 m high and 4.6 m wide, hence the name. It is surrounded by natural beech forest, with skunk cabbage in late spring and autumn colours.

sights.name: Akayu Onsen
sights.description: A hot-spring town opened more than 930 years ago and once visited by Uesugi lords. Six wineries, some offering tastings, stand in the grape-growing district, and the town is known for spicy miso ramen.

sights.name: Eboshiyama Hachimangu Shrine
sights.description: A shrine in Akayu Onsen, Nanyo, with a jointless single-stone torii. Its sacred rope is replaced each April 18, foliage lasts from mid-October to early November, and a monument honors Suishinshi Masahide.

sights.name: Sosho Park
sights.description: Known for roses and azaleas, and on the Okitama Sakura Corridor. Choyo-zakura and Keikai-zakura are weeping cherries over 150 years old; Choyo was named for the Nanyo view, and Keikai is an old place name.

sights.name: Hase Kannon
sights.name_ja: 珠宮山 宝積坊（真言宗）/ 置賜三十三観音 第30番 長谷観音
sights.description: A Shingon temple and the 30th stop of the Okitama Thirty-three Kannon pilgrimage. The Kannon hall was rebuilt in 1827, and its hidden principal image is a six-shaku standing Sho-Kannon.

sights.name: Yuzuru no Sato Museum
sights.description: A museum in Nanyo's Urushiyama district created to pass on local folktales, including Crane's Gratitude, transmitted as a temple founding story. Displays and oral recitals show how the tales were told in daily life.

sights.name: Lake Tokura
sights.description: A man-made irrigation lake built in the Taisho era; the famous Hanagasa dance is said to have grown from the work songs sung during its construction. Cherry trees line the shore in spring, and migrating birds winter here.

sights.name: Shirogane Falls
sights.description: A 22-meter waterfall marks the entrance to Shirogane Park at the end of Ginzan Onsen. It can appear as two or three streams. A vermilion bridge spans the lip, with an observation deck opposite.

sights.name: Nobesawa Silver Mine Ruins
sights.description: A nationally designated historic site of a silver mine worked from the Muromachi period and abandoned after a collapse in 1689. A lit walkway runs through the tunnel, about 15 minutes from Ginzan Onsen.

sights.name: Shirogane-yu
sights.description: A day-trip communal bath in Ginzan Onsen, housed in a modern building by Kengo Kuma and Associates. It recalls the feel of the town's former hot-spring cure days.

sights.name: Ginzan Onsen (Autumn Foliage)
sights.description: From the hot-spring street, a walking course to Shirogane Falls and the silver-mine cave can also be done in yukata.

sights.name: Shirogane Park
sights.description: A park in Ginzan Onsen that includes Yoshino cherries, a mountain-cherry park area, Omokage Garden, a rest house, and toilets.

sights.name: Basho and Seifu Historical Museum (Suzuki Family Residence)
sights.name_en: Basho and Seifu Historical Museum (Suzuki Family Residence)
sights.name_ja: 芭蕉、清風歴史資料館(鈴木家住宅)
sights.description: Opened in July 1983, this Edo-period townhouse has hanging fireproof lattice doors and a snow-country central-gate plan with a through earthen floor. Permanent and special exhibitions, lectures, and gallery talks are held.

sights.name: Showakan
sights.description: Located in Ginzan, Obanazawa City, in the Murayama area.

sights.name: Gosho no Mizu Park Lotus Flower Field
sights.name_en: Gosho no Mizu Park Lotus Flower Field
sights.name_ja: 御所の水公園 ハスの花畑
sights.description: About 10,000 lotus plants grow across 3.5 hectares of fallow rice fields. In summer, visitors can enjoy the cool flowing spring water of Gosho no Mizu and take some home.

sights.name: Mount Gosho
sights.name_ja: 御所山(鶴子口層雲峡、クラビ、南御所山縦走、荒神)
sights.description: The Sounkyo course has gorge scenery with many places worth seeing. Dwarf pine carpets the summit, which has views, and mountain vegetables and mushrooms grow in spring, summer and autumn.

activities.name: Oku-Oe Yanagawa Onsen
activities.description: Also called Netsu no Yu, this spring retains heat well and is used for arteriosclerosis and chronic skin conditions. Drinking, day bathing, and a foot bath are possible, with hydrangeas beside the open-air bath.

activities.name: Therme Hakuryo Health Onsen Hall
activities.name_ja: テルメ柏陵健康温泉館
activities.description: Hot-spring health facility on the Mogami River bank in Oe, sourced from Funauta Onsen. The water is a sulfur-bearing sodium-calcium chloride spring, used for diabetes, neuralgia, and muscle pain.

activities.name_en: Daisen Nature Park Cottages and Campground
activities.name_ja: 大山自然公園コテージ・キャンプ場
activities.description: Children can play on the lawn plaza. Seasonal plants include satozakura in early to mid-May, hime-sayuri lilies from late May to early June, and hydrangeas from late June to late July.

activities.name: Daisen Nature Park
activities.description: Satoyama park on the 317 m summit of Mt. Daisen, southwest of JR Aterazawa Station. Plaza and observation building views include the Asahi range, Mt. Gassan, the Ou Mountains, and the Murayama Basin.

activities.name: Jindai Kaya
activities.description: About 1,500 years old, this kaya has a legend that its spirit and a cedar 8 m around, before nearby Miroku-do, traveled together to Ise. Tradition forbids cutting it even if dead.

activities.name: Filming Location of "Isha Sensei" (Fujita, Oe)
activities.name_ja: 映画「いしゃ」先生ロケ地 （大江町藤田）
activities.description: One filming location for the movie Isha Sensei, which portrays female doctor Shida Chikako and is set in Oisawa, Nishikawa. A later-life scene of Chikako thanking Sojiro was filmed here.

activities.name: Cherry Blossom Light-up at Terme Hakuryo Health Onsen
activities.name_en: Cherry Blossom Light-up at Terme Hakuryo Health Onsen
activities.name_ja: テルメ柏陵健康温泉館桜ライトアップ
activities.description: Cherry trees planted around the facility are lit up in mid-April at full bloom. The baths are 100 percent free-flowing source water, where visitors can ease daily fatigue as spring arrives.

activities.name: Roadside Station Shiroi Mori Oguni
activities.description: Located 5 km east of the Niigata border along Route 113, with a light-meal and rest corner, restaurant, and local-products shop. It adjoins Yokone Ski Area, with skiing and snowboarding in winter.

activities.name: Wakasagi Fishing Experience
activities.description: Fish for wakasagi on snow-covered Shiroi Mori Oguni Lake. Rods can be rented from a hut, and about 2,000 people of all ages visit during the season.

activities.name: Mamino-taira Chestnut Orchard
activities.description: In the Kaname district, this 4-hectare orchard has 1,000 chestnut trees. Visitors gather chestnuts in autumn from late September to late October; falling time can shift with the weather.

activities.name: Kurosawa-toge Stone-Paved Road
activities.description: Mossy paving stones laid in 1512 as part of the Echigo Kaido served transport and trade. About 3,600 remain nearly intact over 2.7 km to Shinono; the road is a town cultural property.

activities.name: Nukumidaira Beech Forest Mini Tour
activities.name_ja: ブナの森 温身平（ぬくみだいら）ミニツアー（8月～10月の日・祝）実施
activities.description: Nukumidaira stands at the foot of the Iide Range. White beech trunks and snow give the town its White Forest name. A forest-therapy attendant is stationed at the entrance on Sundays and holidays, August to October.

activities.name: Shiroimori Auto Campground
activities.name_ja: 白い森オートキャンプ場
activities.description: Campground among Asahi range greenery and the Arakawa River, with showers and toilets. Guests can use indoor baths at adjacent Rifure, play in the river, or walk the forest.

activities.name: Matagi no Sato Exchange Hall
activities.name_ja: マタギの郷 交流館
activities.description: Exhibition room on matagi history and culture, in the Kodamagawa district where that culture has long been passed down. A restaurant serves meals made with local ingredients.

activities.name: Buna no Mori Nukumidaira Retreat Tour: Forest Nap and Tea Time
activities.name_en: Buna no Mori Nukumidaira Retreat Tour: Forest Nap and Tea Time
activities.name_ja: ブナの森 温身平リトリートツアー 森の中でお昼寝・ティータイム
activities.description: Forest therapy attendants guide visitors through a beech forest of trees over 200 years old, on seasonal courses that include a nap and tea time.

activities.name: Yokone Health Forest
activities.description: Broadleaf woods of beech, oak, chestnut, magnolia and maple cover about 180 hectares. Walking trails total 8.6 km, and bungalows and an exchange center stand in the forest.

sights.description: The most striking part of the Arakawa Gorge in Bandai-Asahi National Park, near the Niigata border. Its slopes of maple and beech turn red in autumn, earning it the name 'Japan's Red Cliffs'.

sights.name: Lone Cherry Tree of Taruguchi Pass
sights.name_en: Lone Cherry Tree of Taruguchi Pass
sights.description: A solitary Oyamazakura cherry tree near the summit of Taruguchi Pass blooms from late April to early May while snow remains. A nearby deck looks across the Iide mountain range.

day_to_day.name_ja: 肘折名物「肘折朝市」
day_to_day.description: This morning market is one of Hijiori Onsen's local specialties. It runs daily from April 20 to early December, selling seasonal wild vegetables and produce, and many visitors come to talk with local women.

day_to_day.name_ja: 大蔵村観光協会（肘折いでゆ館内）
day_to_day.description: Inside Hijiori Ideyu-kan, the association introduces lodgings suited to each visitor and answers sightseeing and other questions.

day_to_day.name_en: Hijiori Ideyu Hall (Okura Village Tourism Association)
day_to_day.name_ja: 肘折いでゆ館（大蔵村観光協会）
day_to_day.description: A core facility in Hijiori Onsen providing tourism and culture information for Okura Village. It includes a cafeteria, rest rooms, coworking space, a Pokemon manhole cover, and a kokeshi and history museum opened in 2026.

activities.name: Hijiori Onsen
activities.description: A hot spring town that still retains the atmosphere of a traditional hot spring resort.

activities.name: Caldera Hot Spring Baths

sights.name: Shikamura Rice Terraces
sights.description: Four mountain hamlets of Okura are known together as Shikamura. Their rice terraces cover about 120 hectares, among the largest in Tohoku, and are listed among Japan's 100 best rice terraces.

sights.name: Okura Yuki Monogatari
sights.description: This snow festival is a winter tradition in Okura Village. The 28th edition includes the Fuyu Hanabi Uchiage, a winter fireworks launch.

sights.name: Jizogura

sights.name: Kaminoyu
sights.description: A communal bath in central Hijiori Onsen using its oldest spring. Separate baths have blue stones on the floor, and a Jizo linked to an onsen legend stands in one corner.

sights.name: Former Hijiori Post Office Building
sights.description: A small landmark in the center of Hijiori Onsen, with window lattices shaped like the postal symbol. The interior cannot currently be viewed, but the building is used for mini-concerts and events.

sights.name: Komatsubuchi
sights.description: A scenic gorge on the Dozan River linked to a legend that samurai Hachiro Koyama of the Shinjo domain slew a giant serpent. Seasonal foliage, including fresh green and autumn leaves, reflects on the water.

sights.name: Beech Forest on National Route 458
sights.description: A beech forest about four kilometers south of Hijiori on National Route 458 forms a tunnel-like passage. Bright new leaves appear in spring, and the landscape turns golden in autumn.

sights.name: Onuma, Naganuma and Bato Kannon
sights.name_ja: 男沼・長沼・馬頭観音
sights.description: Ponds here shelter Ruriitotonbo damselflies and precious aquatic plants and form a designated Yamagata satoyama conservation area. Nearby Bato Kannon, founded in 1727, draws local worship; Naganuma's water level hardly changes through the year.

sights.description: Said to have begun when a fourth-rank court noble built a hall and enshrined a Thousand-Armed Kannon. His descendant, Hino Bitchu no Kami, later ruled the area from a residence on the mountain.

sights.name: Sekisui-zan Saiko-ji (Ji Sect) / Mogami Thirty-three Kannon No. 29 Oishida Kannon

sights.name: Tazawa Pond
sights.description: This pond reflects the shadow of Mount Hayama and is used for fishing as well as by hikers and campers. A Mokichi poem monument stands here.

sights.name: Kawamae Kannon (Mogami 33 Kannon No. 26)

activities.name_ja: 道の駅「寒河江」チェリーランド
activities.description: Along the Sagae River, the grounds include shops for Yamagata products, sweets made with seasonal fruit, and meals using branded beef. Sakuranbo Kaikan on the same site features local cherries and other produce.

activities.name: Sagae Hanasaka Onsen Yu Cherry
activities.name_ja: 寒河江花咲か温泉 ゆ～チェリー
activities.description: Men and women each have three baths of differing spring quality, all using 100% free-flowing source water. The day-trip onsen also has an outdoor bath, sauna, shop, restaurant, and fee-based rest room.

activities.name: Sagae Onsen
activities.description: Roses, a Sagae specialty, float in bath water described as good for the skin. Day-trip bathing includes a rose bath.

activities.name: Park in Sagae
activities.name_ja: 最上川ふるさと総合公園
activities.description: Prefecture-run urban park south of Sagae, opened in April 2000 as Sagae Highway Oasis. It is laid out along the Mogami River and includes cherries, the prefectural tree.

activities.name: Furusawa Shuzo Museum
activities.description: The Furusawa family, said to have been safflower merchants, have long brewed sake in Sagae. Furusawa Shuzo, known for Sawa Masamune, was founded in 1836. Sake was made in the brewery from 1917 to 1983.

activities.name: Grape Picking
activities.description: All-you-can-eat large-grape picking for 60 minutes runs from August 28 until around the end of September. Varieties include Sunny Rouge and Pione.

activities.name: Dewa Three Noted Temples Pilgrimage
activities.description: The three temples are Risshaku-ji in Yamagata City, Jakusho-ji in Tendo City, and Jion-ji in Sagae.

activities.name: Sagae Onsen Foot Bath
activities.description: Seseragi Foot Bath has a hand bath, so hands can be warmed together with the feet.

activities.name: Ninoseki Waterside Park
activities.description: Waterside park next to the urban area, familiar to local residents. In spring, cherry trees along the promenade bloom and it is a blossom-viewing spot in Sagae.

activities.name: Strawberry Picking
activities.description: Visitors pick strawberries in warm tourist-garden greenhouses, even on cold days. Hydroponic growing avoids soil mess, and reservation by the previous day is required.

day_to_day.name: Sakata Seafood Market
day_to_day.description: Right by Sakata Port, selling fish fresh from the Sea of Japan. Sugawara Fish on the ground floor specialises in local catch and can advise on cooking or pack fish to take home, and there is an eat-in corner.

day_to_day.name_ja: 酒田駅
day_to_day.description: A station in Sakata City in the Shonai region of Yamagata.

day_to_day.name_en: Yuyu no Mori Onsen Aiai Hirata
day_to_day.name_ja: 悠々の杜温泉アイアイひらた
day_to_day.description: Day-trip hot-spring facility in a forest, with baths overlooking the Shonai Plain. It burns wood pellets, sells salt extracted from the spring, and has a restaurant and a vegetable shop.

activities.name: Sakata Seafood Market
activities.description: Seafood market beside Sakata Port stocking fish landed from the Sea of Japan. The first-floor Sugawara fish shop focuses on local fish and offers cooking advice and takeaway packing.

activities.name: Chokai Kogen Family Travel Village
activities.description: Leisure facility at 500 meters on the Chokai highlands, with a campsite, cabins, and treehouses for camping-style stays and outdoor barbecues. A ground-golf course in the wide lawn has 48 permanent holes.

activities.name_ja: 雛の飾り菓子制作体験

activities.name: Tatenokawa Brewery
activities.description: Sake brewery founded in 1832 that has contributed to the development of Japan's sake, food, and agriculture culture. Brewery tours are available.

activities.name: Miraini, Sakata Station-Front Exchange Hub
activities.name_ja: 酒田駅前交流拠点施設 ミライニ
activities.description: Miraini is a public facility comprising Sakata City Central Library, the station-front tourist information center, a plaza, municipal parking, and a bus bay.

activities.name: Hiyoriyama Park
activities.description: Sea of Japan sunsets can be seen here. In mid-April, Sakata Hiyoriyama Cherry Blossom Festival features about 400 blooming trees and bonbori night lighting. A wooden hexagonal lighthouse and direction stones stand in the park.

activities.name: Iesaka-tei, Former Sakata Port Shipping Wholesaler
activities.name_en: Iesaka-tei, Former Sakata Port Shipping Wholesaler
activities.name_ja: 酒田湊旧廻船問屋・家坂亭
activities.description: The Iesaka family traded rice and tung oil by kitamaebune from late Edo through mid-Meiji, and made paper raincoats coated with tung oil for sailors. The present building was constructed after the 1894 Shonai Earthquake.

activities.name: Tobishima Seafood Donya
activities.name_ja: 海鮮どんや とびしま
activities.description: On the second floor of Sakata Seafood Market, it serves seafood bowls, limited-quantity boat platters, salmon-roe bowls, and sea-urchin and salmon-roe bowls using seasonal Shonai coast seafood.

activities.name: Sakata Port Cruise
activities.description: A pleasure-boat cruise at Sakata Port. All sailings for the current year were cancelled after an engine failure on the regular ship Tobishima.

activities.name: Hatsumago Sake Brewery Museum Kura Tanbokan
activities.name_en: Hatsumago Sake Brewery Museum Kura Tanbokan
activities.name_ja: 初孫酒造資料館「蔵探訪館」
activities.description: A museum run by Tohoku Meijo, maker of Hatsumago sake, in a black-and-white storehouse amid pines outside Sakata. Exhibits cover brewing history and process, with a tasting corner for seasonal and brewery-only sake.

activities.name: Hachimori Campground
activities.description: A campground in Hachimori Nature Park, with areas for viewing wildflowers, nature observation, and forest bathing. Tents, bungalows, and a cooking area are available, with sports and hot-spring facilities nearby.

sights.description: These functioning rice storehouses form a picturesque view with their black wooden walls lined with a row of Keyaki trees

sights.name: Somaro (Maiko Teahouse and Takehisa Yumeji Museum)
sights.description: The renovated Somaya, Sakata's leading restaurant since the Edo period, reopened in 2000. Its wooden main house was built around surviving storehouses after the 1894 Shonai earthquake fire and is a registered cultural property.

sights.name: Hiyoriyama Park
sights.description: Learn about the historic port town of Sakata at this park with an iconic white lighthouse and traditional white sailing ship!

sights.name: Homma Art Museum
sights.description: The museum's main building, Seienkaku, was built in 1813 and faces the Kakubuen scenic garden, with a new wing completed in 1968. It once hosted the Shonai domain lords and shogunate officials, and later imperial family members.

sights.name: Former Honma Family Residence
sights.description: Feel the spirit of simplicity and fortitude at the residence of Japan’s richest merchant!

sights.name: Sankyo Warehouses Light-Up
sights.name_ja: 山居倉庫のライトアップ
sights.description: Rice storehouses built in 1893, a symbol of rice-growing Shonai, were designated a national historic site in March 2021 and ceased storage in September 2022. Illumination, including under snow, differs from the daytime view.

sights.name: Tsuruma Pond
sights.description: A pond on the way to Mount Chokai's Yunodai trailhead. May greenery and October foliage attract photographers and trekkers, and it is a prefectural natural monument breeding ground for forest green tree frogs.

sights.name: Juni Falls
sights.description: A group of 12 falls in stepped form, with a 30 m drop and a red suspension bridge. The route is fully closed after forest-road damage and landslides as of July 2026.

sights.name: Ken Domon Photography Museum
sights.description: A photography museum opened in 1983 after Ken Domon donated his works to Sakata. Yoshio Taniguchi designed the building, and exhibitions rotate through themes such as temples, Hiroshima, and portraits.

sights.name: Fudo Falls
sights.description: A roughly 15-meter waterfall behind Mitaki Shrine in Shimokurokawa, Sakata, splitting over a projecting rock face. Also called Kaiun Shusse Falls; passage has been closed since heavy rain on 25 July 2024.

sights.name: Kaianji Temple
sights.description: A Soto Zen temple founded in 1394, with Shakyamuni as its principal image. Its three-story pagoda, rebuilt in recent years in traditional style, is one symbol of the town.

sights.name: Daishinji Temple
sights.description: A Jodo Shinshu Honganji-ha temple whose principal image is Amida Nyorai. Founded by Josenbo Ryogen, it moved to the present site in 1624.

sights.name: Maizuru Park
sights.description: A lawn park with an octopus slide, near Yatsumori Nature Park and the Yatsumori Onsen Yurinko day bath. Cherry trees are lit in late April, and the park is used for taro-stew gatherings in October.

sights.name: Former Abumiya
sights.description: A shipping wholesaler's townhouse with a stone-weighted cedar-bark roof, earthen passage, and rows of tatami and board rooms. It prospered in Edo-period Sea of Japan shipping and is mentioned in Ihara Saikaku's Nippon Eitaigura.

sights.name: Sakata Kitako Ryokuchi Observation Deck (Minato Monoshiri-kan)

sights.name_ja: 酒田北港緑地展望台（港ものしり館）
sights.description: Adjoining Sakata Lighthouse since April 2000, the 18-metre deck overlooks the outer and north port, Sea of Japan, and Mount Chokai. The first floor houses Minato Monoshiri-kan, and a nearby plaza has barbecue facilities.

activities.description: The former flatland castle stood within a triple moat; moats and stone walls remain, with Tozawa Shrine, Tenmangu, and Gokoku Shrine. The Tozawa clan ruled the 68,200-koku domain for about 243 years.

activities.name: Yuki no Sato Information Center

activities.description: Forest of about 50 hectares at the foot of Mount Jingamine. The summit is a 50-minute walk from parking, and the path to Higashiyama Gymnasium is part of the Tohoku Nature Trail.

activities.description: Racing kart course 1,063 meters long in Mogami River scenery, for full races and family use. Single-seat karts reach 70 km/h, and the felt speed is said to be about twice that.

activities.name: Kiyokawa Hachiro Memorial Museum
activities.description: Displays relics of Kiyokawa Hachiro, a forerunner of the imperial restoration movement with a major role in the Meiji Restoration. Kiyokawa Shrine and Kanki-ji, with gravestones of Hachiro and his wife Oren, are nearby.

activities.description: Built in 1945-1954, Rokufuchi and Seba are cobblestone-concrete erosion-control dams with curved spillways, now hard to restore. An inscription is carved on the back of the Seba monument.

activities.name: Tateyama Park

activities.description: Past a cave, a stone wall about 30 m high stands at a Takahata-stone quarry. The site is also used for live performances and photo shoots.

activities.name: Hinata Cave
activities.description: Treated as an ogre's rock shelter and kept off-limits in the Edo period; later visitors found stone arrowheads. The cave lies at 230 m on the foothills of a mountain commonly called Tateishi.

activities.name: Yuki no Sato Sansan
activities.description: Log-house-style lodging built with Wada cedar by local craftspeople. Stay essentials are provided, and an agricultural-processing experience facility is also on site.

activities.name: Hamada Hirosuke Memorial Museum
activities.description: Memorial museum for Hamada Hirosuke, a Yamagata children's writer called Japan's Andersen. He published about 1,000 tales and songs over some 50 years, including Naita Aka Oni.

activities.name: Nukanome Waterside School
activities.name_ja: 糠野目 水辺の楽校
activities.description: Riverbed park in Nukanome, once developed by Mogami River boats. A pond about 30 cm deep has stepping stones and a wooden dam for young children, plus a stream and kappa pool from local tales.

activities.name: Yamagata Prefectural Ukitamu Fudoki Hill Archaeological Museum

activities.name_ja: 山形県立うきたむ風土記の丘考古資料館
activities.description: Displays Okitama finds centered on the Oshidashi site. Ukitamu is Okitama's old name in the Nihon Shoki; the area is a Jomon-to-Kofun park and a base for nationally designated caves such as Hinata.

sights.name: Kameoka Monjudo
sights.description: One of Japan's three great Monju temples. A Nio gate with guardian statues stands at the entrance to a cedar-lined approach, and statues of the Sixteen Arhats line the stone path to the main hall.

sights.name: Takahata Winery
sights.description: Among the fruit kingdoms of Yamagata, Takahata Town, where Takahata Winery is located,

sights.name: Former Takahata Station
sights.description: The station building was rebuilt in 1934 in local Takahata stone, unusual for a station. Period trains, tracks, and tools remain on display.

sights.name: Takahata Station
sights.description: A station on the Ou Main Line (Yamagata Line) and Yamagata Shinkansen, unusual for hot-spring facilities in the station building.

sights.name: Akutsu Hachiman Shrine
sights.description: Yamagata's only three-story pagoda, a bugaku hall, and the main hall are prefecture-designated cultural properties along a mossy stone approach. Tradition dates an Amida hall here to 860, but the origin is uncertain.

sights.name: Gyokuryuin Five Hundred Arhat Statues
sights.description: 500 Arhat statues made in Tenpo 6 by Kyoto sculptors fill a Soto Zen hall, with 16 Arhats and 33 Kannon images. They are a town-designated cultural property, each said to have a distinct face.

sights.name: Ichinosawa Cave
sights.description: A nationally designated historic site on a mountainside at 400 meters, northeast of Hiruzawa Lake. Finds show long use and a clear transition from the Incipient Jomon period to the Yayoi period.

sights.name: Shifukuji Temple Site
sights.description: Founded in the Koan era (1278-1287) as a Date academic temple, where young Date Masamune is thought to have studied. After it moved to Sendai in 1591, moats, earthworks, and Date family graves remain.

sights.name: Hatomine Plateau
sights.description: An 800 m pass on the Fukushima border has an 86-hectare pasture where about 100 dairy cows graze each June. Ryugatake (994 m) enshrines a dragon deity, and Hirosuke Hamada's poem monument stands here.

sights.name: Biruzawa Lake
sights.description: A 25-hectare irrigation reservoir begun in 1936 and completed after 13 years. Spring snowmelt fills the green lake, a forest park and Kannon-iwa trail lie nearby, and the Yonezawa-Takahata cycling road ends here.

sights.name: Mahoroba Greenway
sights.name_ja: まほろばの緑道 (高畠駅～まほろば古の里歴史公園)
sights.description: Built on the former Takahata Railway and Yamagata Kotsu Takahata Line, discontinued in 1974, this greenway runs about 6 km and is planted with about 700 cherry trees and seasonal flowers and fruit trees.

sights.name: Wakamatsu-ji Temple
sights.description: Temple No. 1 of the Mogami 33 Kannon pilgrimage (Tendai sect). Legend says the Nara-period priest Gyoki heard a bell on the mountain, climbed it and saw a shining image of Kannon, and founded the temple there.

sights.name: Nakano Fruits (Nakano Tourist Orchard)
sights.description: A popular Tendo orchard offering seasonal fruit picking, with an orchard-run café serving sweets made with fresh fruit; its fruit parfaits and shakes are especially popular.

sights.name: Osho Orchard
sights.description: A fruit-picking orchard with a café, and the only place in Tendo offering greenhouse cherry picking. About 10 hectares of orchards, plus a fruit vending stand open 24 hours a day, all year.

sights.name: Tendo Park Momiji-en Light-up
sights.name_ja: 天童公園もみじ園 ライトアップ
sights.description: A walking-path area linking the Atago-numa waterfront to near Mount Maizuru's summit, lit when cherries and maples are in season. The route is 250 meters long with a 52.4-meter rise and two shelters.

sights.name: Shogi Village Tendo Tower
sights.name_ja: 将棋むら 天童タワー
sights.description: Marked by a giant shogi king piece, it sells decorative pieces and Yamagata specialties and offers shogi writing, soba making, pottery, safflower dyeing and painting. Basho Garden recreates scenic spots visited by Matsuo Basho.

sights.name: Tendo City Museum of Art
sights.description: The collection of Japanese paintings is substantial. About five special exhibitions are held each year, with experience and collection exhibitions between them.

sights.name: Jakushoji Temple
sights.description: Opened by Gyoki in 708 and later rebuilt by Ennin, it is first among the Mogami 33 Kannon temples. A matchmaking rite is held on the first Sunday from April to December, with no reservation needed.

sights.name: Gokurakuen
sights.description: A Japanese garden was built over seven years from 1928 by the late Mitobe Yasaku as unemployment relief. Stone pillars carry sayings on life's joys and sorrows, and the scenery changes by season.

activities.name: Mogami Gorge
activities.description: Sixteen-kilometer gorge on the middle Mogami River, from Furukuchi in Tozawa to Kiyokawa in Shonai. Mountains crowd both banks, and the scenery changes with the seasons.

activities.name: Roadside Station Tozawa Koma-kan
activities.description: Roadside station in Tozawa, known for Mogami River boat cruises. Views from a low hill take in the Mogami River and fields; Korean-style buildings offer Korean ingredients, cosmetics, bibimbap, and cold noodles.
