day_to_day.name_ja: 長寿温泉
day_to_day.description: A public hot-spring bath in a residential district beside Komagihara Park, available in the manner of a neighborhood sento.

activities.name: Atsumi Onsen
activities.description: Atsumi Onsen is a hot spring resort town with a pleasant atmosphere.

activities.name: Kushibiki Taranokidai Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: 櫛引たらのきだいスキー場
activities.description: A ski area with courses from beginner to intermediate and advanced levels. Daytime views take in the Shonai Plain and the Sea of Japan, and night skiing overlooks the lights of Tsuruoka.

activities.name: Yudonosan Ski Resort
activities.description: Four courses range from a 300 m advanced run (35-degree maximum slope) to a gentle 2,000 m forest course. The slopes include a terrain park and R-shaped walls, plus a ski and snowboard school.

activities.name: Hachimoriyama Ski Area
activities.description: Tsuruoka's ski area closest to the Sea of Japan, with a T-bar lift. Its hut is open free as a rest stop, and the slope can be seen from the Nihonkai-Tohoku Expressway.

activities.name: Picture Candle Painting Experience
activities.name_ja: 絵ろうそく絵付け体験
activities.description: At Togashi Candle Shop, visitors paint historic picture candles once presented to the Tokugawa shogunate, also called flower-crest candles. Staff teach delicate hand-painted pigment patterns, and a candle can be finished in about one hour.

activities.name: Hagurosan Ski Area
activities.description: A ski area in Tsuruoka with views of Mount Gassan. It has beginner, intermediate and advanced courses and a separate slope for small children.

activities.name: Stained Glass Making Experience
activities.name_ja: ステンドグラス製作体験
activities.description: At a workshop opposite Tsuruoka Catholic Church, visitors make stained-glass lampshades and kaleidoscopes with a soldering iron. Sessions take about two hours and accept elementary-school age and up.

activities.name: Soba-Making Experience at Furusato Mura Takaradani
activities.name_en: Soba-Making Experience at Furusato Mura Takaradani
activities.name_ja: そば打ち体験／ふるさとむら宝谷
activities.description: Visitors make and eat fresh handmade soba from locally grown buckwheat milled on a stone mill. Local farmers guide the session, so beginners can take part, and pickles and tempura use local ingredients.

activities.name: Sososo Camp Nezugaseki Campground
activities.name_ja: そそそCAMP～鼠ヶ関キャンプ場
activities.description: A seaside campground with the sea in front, where visitors can enjoy rock-pool play and rock fishing. Nearby are Marine Park Nezugaseki beach, Benten Island, Nezugaseki Lighthouse, and Nezugaseki fishing port.

activities.name: Yamabushi Ascetic Training Experience
activities.description: Wearing white robes, participants leave daily life to try part of yamabushi training and learn about Dewa Sanzan—Mt. Haguro, Mt. Gassan, and Mt. Yudono—and Shugendo.

sights.name: Mt. Haguro
sights.description: One of the Three Mountains of Dewa, with Mount Gassan and Mount Yudono, revered as sacred mountains for hundreds of years. Travel to them is said to be a journey of reincarnation.

sights.name: Kamo Aquarium
sights.description: Awarded a Guinness World Record for the world’s largest jellyfish collection

sights.name: Mt. Gassan
sights.description: Enjoy breath-taking views while trekking on this mountain judging reincarnation

sights.name: Mt. Haguro Dewa Sanzan Sanjin Gosaiden
sights.description: The Sanjin Gosaiden on the summit of Mt. Haguro enshrines the deities of all three Dewa Sanzan mountains: Gassan, for peace after death (the past); Haguro, for happiness in this life (the present); and Yudono, for rebirth (the future).

sights.name: Yudonosan Shrine
sights.description: This mysterious sacred location is the last stop of the Three Mountains of Dewa

sights.name: Yunohama Onsen
sights.description: Hot spring hotels face the Sea of Japan, with sunset views from open-air baths.

sights.name: Mt. Yudono
sights.description: At 1,504 m and linked to Mt. Gassan, Mt. Yudono ranks with Ise and Kumano as one of Japan's three great sacred sites. In a gorge carved by the Bonji River on its northern slope stands the main sanctuary of Yudonosan Shrine, revered as a guardian of good harvests and household safety.

sights.name: Haguro-san Five-Story Pagoda
sights.name_ja: （国宝）羽黒山 五重塔 【12年分のご利益！ 令和８年「羽黒山午年御縁年」】
sights.description: A 29-meter unpainted five-story pagoda in a cedar avenue on the Mount Haguro approach, designated a National Treasure in 1966. Said to have been rebuilt about 600 years ago, it stands near giant cedar Jiji-sugi.

sights.name: Gassan Eighth Station Midagahara
sights.name_ja: 月山八合目 弥陀ヶ原
sights.description: An alpine wetland at 1,400 m on Gassan, with more than 130 alpine plant species, including Nikko daylilies and skunk cabbage. A boardwalk loop of about 60 minutes can be reached by bus.

sights.name: Honmyoji Temple
sights.description: It enshrines self-mummified monk Honmyo Kai Shonin, the oldest of six in Shonai, preserved with little damage and said to reflect strict wood-eating asceticism. A meditation mound and believers' monuments remain beside the hall.

sights.name: Zenpoji Temple
sights.description: A Soto Zen dragon-god temple with Japan's only fish-scale memorial five-story pagoda. It keeps an 1833 Dragon King Hall, 1855 arhat hall, 1862 gate and Hishida Shunso's Important Cultural Property painting.

sights.name: Dewa Sanzan Shrine
sights.description: A shrine on the summit of Mount Haguro jointly enshrining the deities of Mount Gassan, Mount Haguro, and Mount Yudono. Year-round rites for the three shrines are held here together.

sights.name: Nanatsu Falls
sights.description: A 90-meter tiered waterfall on the Rokujurigoe Road in Bandai-Asahi National Park, one of Japan's 100 Waterfalls. Full view is visible from Nanatsu Falls Park, with fresh greenery and autumn leaves.

sights.name: Chido Museum
sights.description: A museum in the former Sakai residence at Tsuruoka Castle's third bailey. Relocated buildings include the old Nishitagawa County Office, and the Sakai Clan Garden is a national Place of Scenic Beauty.

sights.name: Zuishinmon Gate
sights.description: The front entrance to the sacred precinct of Dewa Sanzan Shrine, enshrining gate deities that keep evil out. Called the Niomon until the Meiji era, it was donated in 1695 by the lord of Yashima.

sights.name: Yudonosan Churenji Temple
sights.name_ja: 湯殿山 注連寺（真言宗 智山派）/ 庄内三十三観音 第31番
sights.description: Founded by Kobo Daishi as a distant-worship site for women once barred from Yudonosan. This Shingon Chizan temple enshrines the self-mummified monk Tetsumonkai Shonin and is the 31st of the Shonai Thirty-Three Kannon.

sights.name: Tsuruoka Park
sights.description: A park on the former Tsurugaoka Castle site, seat of the Sakai family for about 250 years. Moats, stone walls, and centuries-old cedars remain, with 730 cherry trees among Japan's 100 cherry sites.

sights.name: Gassan Hanagasa Line
sights.description: A scenic drive along the former Rokujurigoe Kaido, once a pilgrimage road to Dewa Sanzan. Fresh greenery and autumn leaves are beautiful, with viewpoints and sights along the route.

sights.name: Nezugaseki
sights.description: A coastal area in southwestern Tsuruoka on the Niigata border, said to be where Basho passed a checkpoint. The prefectural boundary runs through the built-up area, and fishing-town events are held.

sights.name: Gassan Dam
sights.description: The dam office information hall on Lake Asahi Gassan shows fish from the Aka River and models of the dam. An observation deck overlooks the lake, and interior dam tours are offered.

sights.name: Yamairagawa Tamasugi Cedar
sights.description: On the grounds of Kumano Shrine in Yamairagawa, this cedar is said to be over 1,500 years old. About 36 m tall with a hemispherical crown, it was designated a national natural monument in 1951.

sights.name: Dewa Sanzan Historical Museum
sights.description: Displays many materials on Haguro-san ascetic practice and faith, including 190 of 500 bronze mirrors unearthed from Kagami-ike and Buddhist statues, plus old documents related to Matsuo Basho.

sights.name: Oyama Park
sights.description: A park on the site of Oura Castle, seat of the Muto clan, completed in 1940. It has two lookouts and eight monuments, and is known for cherry blossoms and seasonal hydrangeas.

sights.name: Kumano Shrine (Tsuruoka)
sights.description: Said to date from 672, when En no Gyoja enshrined a deity atop Mount Atsumi. Moved here in 1916, it was rebuilt in 1958 after the 1950 Atsumi Onsen fire.

sights.name: Gassan Nakanomiya Mitahara Sanrojo
sights.name_ja: 月山中の宮 御田原参篭所
sights.description: A prayer facility a 10-minute walk from the parking area at the eighth station of Mount Gassan. It accepts prayers and memorial services, but not lodging or meals.

sights.name: Studio Sedic Shonai Open Set
sights.name_ja: スタジオセディック庄内オープンセット
sights.description: A film studio open to the public where many movies and dramas were shot. A 2 km site holds post-town, fishing-village, farming-village, and mountain-settlement sets, plus photo displays and play areas.

sights.name: Yura Onsen
sights.description: A coastal onsen area. Hakusan Island, its symbol, is reached by a vermilion bridge and has a fishing pond and a 40- to 60-minute loop; the bridge is lit in summer.

sights.name: Hagurozan Shozen-in Temple
sights.name_ja: 羽黒山 正善院（羽黒山 修験本宗）/ 庄内三十三観音 第1番
sights.description: A Haguro Shugendo temple, said to have been founded by Jikaku Daishi, and the first stop on the Shonai 33 Kannon pilgrimage. Its Golden Hall, a national Important Cultural Property, houses 33 gilded Kannon statues.

sights.name: Marine Park Nezugaseki Beach
sights.name_ja: マリンパークねずがせき海水浴場
sights.description: A low-turbidity gravel beach with calm waves, listed by the Environment Ministry among 100 bathing beaches. It includes an artificial rocky shore, lawn and dusk views of Benten Island and the Japan Sea.

sights.name: Nenju no Matsu Garden
sights.description: A black pine in a 20-meter reclining-dragon form was planted about 400 years ago. Designated a Yamagata Prefecture natural monument in 1955, the present garden was completed in 1994 to a design by Ken Nakajima.

sights.name: Yokozuna Kashiwado Memorial Hall
sights.description: Built to honor Kashiwado, Tsuruoka honorary citizen and 47th yokozuna of the Showa Kashiwado-Taiho era. The former Kagamiyama stable practice ring and raised room from Tokyo were relocated here, with memorabilia and match videos.

sights.name: Kasuga Shrine
sights.description: Said to have been founded in 806, early in the Heian period. It is known as the shrine where Kurokawa Noh, a nationally designated Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property, is performed.

sights.name: Yuzusame Shrine
sights.description: Worshipped as Yudagawa Onsen's guardian and as a deity of hot springs and water. A prefecture-designated natural monument, a giant milk ginkgo, stands by the stone steps, and the grounds hold memorial poem stones.

sights.name: Sugake Garden
sights.description: Garden of the house granted to Sanehide Suge, a late-Edo to Meiji Shonai retainer who knew Takamori Saigo. Mid-Edo style remains, with a 350-year-old pine, weeping cherry, azaleas, and a shrine to Sugawara no Michizane.

sights.name: Shonai Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 1877 on the former main bailey of Tsurugaoka Castle by people who revered the Sakai lords. A treasure hall shows related arms, crafts, and seasonal dolls, and seasonal flowers decorate a hand-water basin.

sights.name: Asahi Mountain Range
sights.description: Ito-dake (1,771.4 m) is the northern start and end of the traverse and overlooks Otori Pond, a 963 m granite lake up to 68 m deep, linked to the legendary fish Takitaro.

sights.name: Great Torii
sights.description: A vermilion ryobu torii, 20 m high and 15 m wide, marks entry to Dewa Sanzan. Donated in 1929 by Tetsutaro Yoshioka of Yamagata City, the slope beyond is called Shinjizaka.

sights.name: Kinbozan Shoryu-ji Temple
sights.name_ja: 金峯山 青龍寺（真言宗 豊山派）/ 庄内三十三観音 第33番
sights.description: A Shingon Buzan-school temple and the 33rd stop of the Shonai Thirty-three Kannon pilgrimage. It enshrines Nyoirin Kannon, and Kinbozan is a prefecture-designated scenic site with a shrine.

sights.name: Atsumi Onsen Rose Garden
sights.description: A rose garden on high ground overlooking the Atsumi Onsen town, planted with about 90 varieties and 3,000 bushes that bloom from June to October. A rose festival is held each June.

sights.name: Oguni Castle Ruins
sights.description: Mountain-castle ruins on Tateyama (348.5 m), about 10 km southwest of JR Atsumi Onsen Station, estimated to date from the 14th century and abandoned in 1615. Earthwork ramparts on the summit are considered unusual.

sights.name: Yamagata-Niigata Prefecture Border Marker
sights.description: A stone monument on the border between Yamagata and Niigata prefectures. It blends into a residential street so fully that the border is easy to miss, and it has appeared on Tetsuwan DASH.

sights.name: Sanze Beach
sights.description: A swimming beach near Route 7, with varied strange rocks and a natural rock diving platform. It is popular with families, photographers visit for the Tateiwa sunset, and it was a film location.

sights.name: Benten Island
sights.description: Tradition says Minamoto no Yoshitsune landed by boat at Nezugaseki while fleeing to Ou. Itsukushima Shrine stands on the island, and a promenade overlooks the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Tsuruoka City Shuhei Fujisawa Memorial Museum
sights.name_en: Tsuruoka City Shuhei Fujisawa Memorial Museum
sights.name_ja: 鶴岡市立藤沢周平記念館
sights.description: Exhibits manuscripts, materials, and personal items of historical novelist Shuhei Fujisawa and recreates his Tokyo study. It also presents the Kaisaka Domain, said to model Edo-period Shonai, plus local nature and history in his works.

sights.name: Nezugaseki Itsukushima Shrine
sights.description: The shrine stands on Benten Island, a scenic spot in Nezugaseki, Tsuruoka, and enshrines Ichikishima-hime. Its mikoshi-nagashi festival is held every April 15, and a path leads to Nezugaseki Lighthouse.

sights.name: Kinsei Nenju-zeki Site
sights.description: The present checkpoint site is where ancient Nezumigaseki was moved. It is said to have been developed after the Sakai clan entered Shonai in 1622, though the circumstances and timing remain unclear.

sights.name: Mount Haguro Minamidani
sights.description: Ruins of the branch temple Shionji, where Basho stayed, built about 300 years ago. Foundation stones and a pond garden remain; it is a prefectural historic site and one of Japan's 100 Scent Landscapes.

sights.name: Local sight in Tsuruoka (#2)
sights.name_ja: 早田のオハツキイチョウ
sights.description: A ginkgo whose seeds grow on the tips of its fan-shaped leaves, a form confirmed in only about 20 trees in Japan. It was designated a national natural monument in 1951.

sights.name: Chotokuji Temple
sights.description: Said to have begun during 1345-1349 after an Amida statue was found glowing in a tree. It is the seventh Shonai pilgrimage site and later held a temple school, an onsen school, and a nursery.

sights.name: Daitokuji Temple
sights.description: Grave site of the Shonai domain's Sakai family lords, enclosed by black wooden fences. A monument calls it the birthplace of school lunches, after Meiji-era priests here fed children from poor families.

sights.name: Former Kazama Family Residence Heishindo
sights.description: A merchant house built in 1896 by the Kazama family, Shonai domain purveyors, on a former samurai-residence site. The stone-weighted roof holds about 40,000 stones; the house is a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Gassan Kogen Harmony Park
sights.name_ja: 月山高原ハーモニーパーク
sights.description: A plaza inside Gassan Kogen Ranch, with about 100 hectares of lawn where cattle and sheep graze. On clear days an observation deck looks over Mount Gassan, Mount Haguro, Mount Chokai, and the Shonai Plain.

sights.name: Atsumi Onsen Atsumigawa Riverbank
sights.name_ja: あつみ温泉 温海川河畔
sights.description: A riverside walk along the Atsumi River through Atsumi Onsen, with cherry blossoms in spring, sweetfish fishing in summer and a salmon run in autumn. A waterside foot bath and wooden deck line the path.

sights.name: Mount Atsumi
sights.description: A 736-meter mountain about 2 km northeast of Atsumi Onsen, with a Kumano Shrine hall and a driveable summit road. Clear days bring views of Mount Chokai, the Shonai coast, and Sado Island.

sights.name: Mount Haguro Cedar Avenue
sights.description: More than 500 cedars aged 350 to 500 years, a national special natural monument, line the roughly 2 km approach and 2,446 stone steps. The walk to Sanjin Gosaiden takes about 60 minutes.

sights.name: Local sight in Tsuruoka (#1)
sights.description: A visitor hall at the foot of Mount Ito, with exhibits on the legendary giant fish Takitaro of Otori Pond and Asahi range hiking information. It includes a cafeteria, cafe, and fishing pond.

sights.name: Kurokawa Noh no Sato Ogi Hall
sights.name_en: Kurokawa Noh no Sato Ogi Hall
sights.description: A facility introducing Kurokawa Noh, a nationally designated Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property. Life-size dolls recreate the Ogi Festival child dance, and four programs are shown on a large screen.

sights.name: Mount Hachimori
sights.description: Seasonal activities here include wild-vegetable gathering in spring, camping in summer, hiking in autumn, and skiing in winter.

sights.name: Mount Takadate
sights.description: A 274-metre beech and oak mountain, a Forestry Agency recreational forest and one of 100 forest-bathing woods, has paths. New leaves show mid-May to June, and lotus covers Kamiike pond from late July to mid-August.

sights.name: Yamagata Prefectural Cultural and Arts Hall
sights.name_en: Yamagata Prefectural Cultural and Arts Hall
sights.name_ja: 山形県総合文化芸術館
sights.description: A cultural complex at JR Yamagata Station's west exit, centered on a 2,001-seat hall and finished with local crafts. A shop sells goods from 35 municipalities, and a restaurant uses prefectural ingredients.

sights.name: Zao Onsen Large Open-Air Bath
sights.description: A rustic streamside open-air bath in Zao Onsen, using a strongly acidic sulfur spring. Showers, soap, and shampoo are not available, and metal jewelry should be removed because the water corrodes it.

sights.name: Omoshiroyama Momijigawa Gorge
sights.description: A gorge below Mount Omoshiroyama on the Yamagata-Miyagi border, with a roughly 2 km trail, waterfalls, and a suspension bridge. Autumn colors the trees red and yellow; the path is narrow and can be slippery.

sights.name: Yamadera Basho Memorial Museum
sights.description: A Japanese-style museum on a hill overlooking Yamadera, built to mark 300 years since Basho's visit. It displays his original writings; the rear lookout shows Risshaku-ji in cherry blossom, summer green, autumn leaves, and snow.

sights.name: Kurosawa Onsen
sights.description: A quiet hot-spring district that opened in 1970 among farmland.

sights.name: Kajo Central
sights.description: A public-private tenant building that opened on January 1, 2001 at the west exit of Yamagata Station. An observation floor occupies the top level.

sights.name: Zao Onsen Communal Baths
sights.description: Three communal baths, Kamiyu, Shimoyu, and Kawarayu, are located in the Zao Onsen district. Shimoyu has a foot bath.

sights.name: Yamagata Prefectural Museum
sights.description: Opened in 1971 inside Kajo Park on the Yamagata Castle site, it presents prefectural nature, history, and culture through geology, plants, animals, archaeology, history, and folklore. An education-materials annex and nature study garden are attached.

sights.name: Zao Central Highlands
sights.description: A highland plateau in the Zao Onsen area of Yamagata City, with marshes such as Dokko Marsh, Mount Torikabuto, and a primeval beech forest.

sights.name: Yamagata Sake Museum and Yukemuri Yatai Tsumami
sights.name_en: Yamagata Sake Museum and Yukemuri Yatai Tsumami
sights.name_ja: 山形酒のミュージアム＆湯けむり屋台つまみ
sights.description: In Zao Onsen, visitors compare sakes from Yamagata breweries and look for a bottle that suits them. An attached stall serving imoni and other dishes is currently closed.

sights.name: Hasedo Castle Ruins Park
sights.description: A park at the Hasedo Castle ruins and castle mountain in Yamagata City. Volunteer guides cover historic sites in the park.

sights.name: Yamagata Prefectural Industrial Science Museum
sights.description: Exhibits introduce advanced technology from prefectural companies and let visitors try scientific principles. Hands-on devices cover the environment, a corner offers simple crafts, and panels on a spiral staircase trace the prefecture's industrial history.

sights.name: Yamagata Museum of Art
sights.description: Beside the East Otemon Gate of Kajo Park, it shows special exhibitions plus permanent displays of Edo-to-modern Japanese art, local art, and French paintings. It is also used for presentations by local cultural groups.

sights.name: Mamigasaki Sakura Line
sights.name_ja: 馬見ヶ崎さくらライン
sights.description: About 200 cherry trees line the embankment of the Mamigasaki River, forming a blossom tunnel along the riverside path in spring. Part of the row is illuminated at night.

sights.name: Seifuso
sights.description: Stands in Momiji Park, a pond-stroll garden, and has an attached tea room called Hokoan.

sights.name: Yamagin Kenmin Hall Event Plaza

sights.name_en: Yamagata Prefectural Museum Annex Education Materials Hall
sights.name_ja: 山形県立博物館分館 教育資料館
sights.description: Opened in 1980 in the former Yamagata Normal School main building, constructed in 1901 and designated a national Important Cultural Property. Exhibits cover the history of education in Yamagata.

sights.name: Nishizao Park
sights.description: A park in a nature-rich setting, with athletic play equipment, a campground, a barbecue area, and an observation plaza.

sights.name: Zao Daigongen
sights.description: A worship hall for Zao Daigongen of Shimotakarazawa (Zao-guchi), Yamagata City, built in front of Zao Sky Cable Central Plateau Station.

sights.name_ja: 山形駅東西自由通路「アピカ」
sights.description: An east-west passage at Yamagata Station running in front of the ticket gates. It has a book plaza, coin lockers, and display cases, and is used for events and exhibitions.

sights.name: Mutsukunugisan Sofuku-in Temple
sights.name_ja: 六椹山 宗福院（天台宗）/ 最上三十三観音 第8番 六椹観音
sights.description: A Tendai temple, the eighth of the Mogami Thirty-three Kannon, traditionally founded by Gyoki and revived by Jikaku Daishi. Fire walking is held on February 3, and a lantern memorial service on August 9.

sights.name: Yamagata City Nishi Park
sights.description: A park in western Yamagata City developed as greenery meant to absorb and store carbon dioxide. It is a place for environmental learning about plants and wildlife and for health activities among the trees.

sights.name: Former Yoshiike Clinic
sights.description: A building of high historic value that Yamagata City preserves and uses. It is open to the public only when events are held.

sights.name: Arare Falls
sights.description: A segmented waterfall of about 10 meters at the foot of Bishamon-kura's huge rock wall, in an open area. It is seen from the Momiji River gorge path, about 15 minutes from the parking space.

sights.name: Shukokuzan Kisshoin Temple
sights.name_ja: 守国山 吉祥院（天台宗）/ 最上三十三観音 第3番 千手堂観音
sights.description: A Tendai temple known as Senjudo Kannon, the third of the Mogami 33 Kannon. Its main image is a national Important Cultural Property that survived a 1531 fire, and the grounds include a lotus pond.

sights.description: One of Japan's 100 best waterfalls: 80 m high and 40 m wide, among the largest in Tohoku. A viewing platform is about 30 minutes' climb up the trail from Namegawa Onsen.

sights.description: A famous waterfall in Shirabu Onsen(Shirabu Hot spring). The majestic appearance with a height of 30m is quite spectacular.

sights.name: Kasugasan Rinsenji Temple
sights.description: The Uesugi family temple of the Yonezawa domain, founded by Nagao Yoshikage, grandfather of Uesugi Kenshin. It was first built at the foot of Kasugayama Castle in present-day Joetsu, Niigata, and moved to Yonezawa with the clan.

sights.name: Toko no Sakagura Sake Brewing Museum
sights.name_en: Toko no Sakagura Sake Brewing Museum
sights.name_ja: 酒造資料館 東光の酒蔵
sights.description: A sake museum in Yonezawa at Kojima Sohonten, founded in 1597 as a purveyor to the Yonezawa domain's Uesugi family. The brewery shop offers tastings, including higher-grade and award-winning sake.

sights.name: Tengendai Plateau
sights.description: A 1,300-meter plateau in Yonezawa with clear-day views toward Zao, Chokai, Gassan, Iide, and Asahi, and a short approach to Mount Azuma. Trekking, autumn foliage, and skiing from late November into Golden Week are available.

sights.name: Uesugi Memorial Hall (Former Uesugi Count's Residence)
sights.name_en: Uesugi Memorial Hall (Former Uesugi Count's Residence)
sights.name_ja: 上杉記念館（旧上杉伯爵邸）
sights.description: First built in 1896 and rebuilt in cypress in 1925 after the Yonezawa fire, this former count's residence is a registered cultural property. It serves the local dish katemono beside a garden modeled on Hama-rikyu.

sights.name: Uesugi Family Mausoleum
sights.description: Tombs of Yonezawa's successive Uesugi lords, from Kenshin to the 12th lord Narisada, stand among cedars. Kenshin's remains were moved here in 1876; snow lanterns are set out in mid-February.

sights.name: Mount Nishi-Azuma
sights.description: The highest peak of the Azuma range stands over 2,000 m on the Fukushima-Yamagata border and is one of Japan’s 100 Famous Mountains. The Tengendai Ski Area ropeway and lift make the ascent relatively easy.

sights.name: Domori Zenkoji Temple
sights.description: A temple linked to Maeda Keiji, said to have kept a hermitage here late in life, with a memorial tower on the grounds. It holds prefecture-designated Buddhist statues and is planted with hydrangeas.

sights.name: Onariyama Park
sights.description: A hilltop park with 1,000 cherry trees in spring. An observation deck looks over Yonezawa and mountains including Azuma, Zao, and Oasahi, and the grounds include a ski area and ski jumps.

sights.name: Soryukyo Lookout (Aka Falls and Kuro Falls)
sights.name_en: Soryukyo Lookout (Aka Falls and Kuro Falls)
sights.name_ja: 双竜峡展望台（赤滝・黒滝）
sights.description: Aka Falls and Kuro Falls are seen at a distance from a lookout just past the Nishi-Azuma Tunnel. Both are 100-meter branching falls, viewable from June to early November.

sights.name: Onogawa Onsen Firefly Park
sights.name_ja: 小野川温泉ほたる公園
sights.description: A park about 200 meters from the onsen district where fireflies fly from mid-June to mid-July. Viewing is most suitable around 8 to 9 p.m.

sights.name: Local sight in Yonezawa
sights.description: A museum of over 700 archaeological, historical, and folk items from Yonezawa and Okitama, gathered by former director Miyasaka Zensuke. It includes 56 armor suits, some attributed to Uesugi, Naoe, and Maeda lords.

sights.name: Former Yonezawa Higher Technical School Main Building
sights.name_en: Former Yonezawa Higher Technical School Main Building
sights.name_ja: 旧米沢高等工業学校本館
sights.description: Opened in 1910 and designated an Important Cultural Property in 1973, it is a Renaissance-style wooden two-story building. It is the only structure on the Yamagata University engineering campus that retains the school's original appearance.

sights.name: Shirako Shrine
sights.description: It enshrines two kami, a fire deity and Haniyamahime. City-designated tangible cultural properties here include two Heian-period oni-gawara tiles, two copies of Uesugi Yozan's frugality oath, and a Shirako Daimyojin plaque.

sights.name: Fumon-in

stays.description: Lodging in Onogawa, Yonezawa, with a private open-air free-flowing hot spring bath and room-only stays.

day_to_day.description: A day-use hot spring with a large bath, sauna, and open-air bath fed by two different sources. The sodium chloride water is 38.5 degrees and flows at 800 liters per minute.

activities.name: Michi-no-Eki Chokai Flat
activities.name_ja: 道の駅鳥海 ふらっと
activities.description: Roadside station on National Route 7 with fast food, souvenirs, ramen, and a bakery. The direct-sales shop offers vegetables and processed foods, including Yuza melon, negi, yam, daikon, white eggplant, and kolinky.

activities.name: Kamaiso Beach
activities.description: Fresh water, not seawater, springs from the sand and also wells up on the seabed. Visitors can watch the springs up close and swim in both the sea and the cold spring water.

activities.name: Hands-on craft workshop in Yuza
activities.name_ja: 農林漁業体験実習館「さんゆう」 鳥海山の湧水を堪能♪
activities.description: Hands-on craft workshop in Yuza, Yamagata.

activities.name: Takase Gorge
activities.description: Route at the foot of Mount Chokai spanning Hinokizawa, Babazawa, and Karasawa, with waterfalls and streams. From Fujii, five minutes by car on a forest road reaches parking with a mountain-god shrine.

activities.name: Nishihama Beach
activities.description: Swimming beach on the northern Shonai coast, backed by Mount Chokai, with a straight north-south shoreline, wide white sand, and pine woods. A campground and cottages stand nearby.

activities.name: Nishihama Cottage Village
activities.description: Pots and tableware are provided, so bring personal items, a change of clothes, and food. Families and friends use the cottages for overnight stays, barbecues, and parties, with a pine-forest campsite in front.

activities.name: Salmon Grabbing Contest (2025 Cancelled)
activities.name_ja: 【2025年中止】鮭のつかみどり大会
activities.description: The 30th salmon grabbing contest, scheduled for October 26, was cancelled after a mother bear and cubs were confirmed nearby. Visitor safety was given priority.

activities.name: Nishihama Campground
activities.description: Set in a pine forest, so sun and wind are not a concern. A beach and day-trip onsen are nearby, and families and children's groups use it in summer.

activities.name: Soba-Making Experience at the Foot of Mount Chokai
activities.name_en: Soba-Making Experience at the Foot of Mount Chokai
activities.name_ja: 鳥海山の麓で体験するおもしろ自然塾「そば打ち体験」
activities.description: Soba making with flour grown in the Kanamata district, from mixing water through kneading, rolling, and cutting. Afterward, visitors eat soba that is freshly milled, made, and boiled.

activities.name: Yuza Traditional Sasamaki Making Experience
activities.name_ja: 遊佐の伝統郷土食『笹巻き』づくり体験
activities.description: Sasamaki is a traditional local food passed down in Yuza and made in various shapes. Participants try Yuza’s takenoko-maki form while residents teach each wrapping step.

sights.name: Mt. Chokai
sights.description: Admire the graceful snow-capped mountain from below and enjoy uninterrupted views from the summit!

sights.name: Ichinotaki Falls
sights.description: From a red torii across from the car park, a walk through beech forest leads to Ichinotaki Shrine; iron steps nearby descend to a close view of the roughly 20 m falls, and the trail continues to Ninotaki Falls.

sights.name: Juroku Rakan Rocks
sights.description: Twenty-two Buddhist figures carved into rocks washed by the Japan Sea, completed in 1868 after five years of work begun in 1864. Sixteen arhats are accompanied by Shakyamuni, Manjusri, Samantabhadra, Kannon, and two disciples.

sights.name: Chokai Blue Line
sights.name_ja: 鳥海ブルーライン 2025年4月25日開通
sights.description: A 34.9 km road climbs from sea level to 1,100 m, overlooking Mt. Chokai, the Sea of Japan and the Shonai Plain. Closed early November to late April; snow corridors last late April to mid-May.

sights.name: Dohara Falls
sights.description: Spring water from Mt. Chokai gushes from the rocky slope in two streams said to taste different. The fall drops about 3 m, does not freeze in winter, and the water is untreated.

sights.name: Chokaisan Omonoimi Shrine Fukura Kuchi-no-Miya
sights.name_ja: 鳥海山大物忌神社吹浦口ノ宮
sights.description: Said to date from Emperor Kinmei's 25th year, this is a village shrine of Dewa Province's ichinomiya, whose main sanctuary is on the Mount Chokai summit. Fukura Dengaku is offered on 5 May.

sights.name: Ushiwatari River
sights.description: Spring water from Mount Chokai wells up along the banks of this clear river. On windless days dark green baikamo sways in the current, and salmon run upstream in autumn.

sights.name: Chokai Sanshin Spring
sights.description: A long-used spring on the upper Gekko River in Yuza, reachable by car. Water was piped into the San'yu experience hall, which has a direct-sales shop; Gekko Dam lies along the approach.

sights.name: Chokaisan Omonoimi Shrine Main Hall
sights.name_ja: 鳥海山大物忌神社 本殿
sights.description: The main hall stands at the summit of Mount Chokai, an active volcano revered as Dewa Province's ichinomiya. Tradition dates the shrine to 564, and a 20-year rebuilding, like Ise's, was last held in 1997.

sights.name: Chokaisan Omonoimi Shrine Warabioka Kuchinomiya
sights.name_ja: 鳥海山大物忌神社蕨岡口ノ宮
sights.description: One of two foothill shrines of the summit sanctuary, said to date from Emperor Kinmei's 25th year, more than 1,400 years ago. It enshrines Omonoimi Okami; the May 3 festival is the Omitegura Festival.

sights.name: Sato Seiyo Monument
sights.description: It honors Sato Seiyo (1821–1877) of Yuza, the first Assistant of Railways. He recommended Yokohama for a new port and in 1872 ran Japan's first train from Shimbashi to Yokohama.

sights.name: Former Aoyama Main Residence
sights.description: A Meiji-era mansion built in his hometown of Yuza by Aoyama Tomekichi, who prospered in Hokkaido fisheries. Designated a national Important Cultural Property in 2000, it preserves characteristic Meiji architecture.

sights.name: Kamiko no Mizu
sights.description: Spring water that rises in mountains east of the settlement and was piped in for daily life. It is divided into six tiers, used from drinking water down to washing farm tools.

stays.name_ja: 鳥海温泉 遊楽里
stays.description: Onsen lodging in Yuza, Yamagata.
